articles.title: AI tools were supposed to make students think less, but a major university trial found a different result
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Students scored higher on proctored exams after instructors introduced AI tools tailored to applied STEM courses.
- The trial enrolled 7,200 students across 19 universities, with 4,768 students in the experimental exam analysis.
- The trial compared earlier and later rollouts, leaving open how course-specific tools would perform against generic chatbots.
Students in applied STEM courses scored higher on proctored exams when instructors introduced AI tools tailored to their classes, compared with classes still waiting for their tools, according to a randomized trial across 19 universities reported in a Nov. 14 preprint.
The research led by Jun Li of the University of Michigan estimated a student-level gain of 0.32 standard deviations, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.06 to 0.59 standard deviations.
The estimate puts the improvement at roughly 33% of the typical spread in scores within a class and leaves uncertainty about the size of the gain. Standardizing scores within each class gave researchers a common scale for comparing results across courses that used different exams.
The preregistered trial involved 7,200 students in 55 applied STEM classes over three semesters, from spring 2025 through spring 2026. The study counted each course-and-instructor pairing as one class.
The experimental part of the exam analysis covered 4,768 students across 44 course offerings. Researchers used results from earlier terms alongside that sample to account for how classes had performed before the rollout.
The exam analysis included only proctored, in-person exams, mostly on paper. The remaining exams used strictly monitored computers or restricted-access computers at university testing centers.
The researchers added that screening rule after preregistration and excluded course offerings where exams could allow AI assistance.
What instructors built with AI tools
Researchers grouped classes by subject and academic level, then randomly assigned them to introduce their tools immediately or one teaching term later.
Instructors in both groups received design and technical support, including training sessions, examples of how to write instructions for the tools, and access to a platform to build and deploy them.
Once instructors brought the tools into their courses, all students in those classes had access during the term, before sitting the exams used to measure learning.
Some instructors built tutors that gave students targeted practice and feedback, while others built coaches that guided students through problems by asking questions. Instructors also designed interactive simulations and ran role-play exercises that let students question AI-generated stakeholders.
The study detected no statistically significant change in engagement or satisfaction. Engagement measures varied by class and included records such as attendance and assignment completion, and satisfaction came from end-of-term course evaluations.
The trial compared rollout timing, leaving open how course-specific tools would fare against generic chatbots. How much each design contributed to the gain and whether it extends beyond applied STEM remain open questions.

articles.title: Court Docs Show Breakdown of Tokens Lost in Binance Hack
articles.text:
Binance hackers stole 192 tokens across 11 networks, court docs show
Stablecoins accounted for at least $3.46 billion of the $6.3 billion stolen, while the hackers also took memecoins, tokenized gold and gaming tokens.
Hackers behind the record $6.3 billion Binance hack stole a total of 192 cryptocurrencies across 11 blockchain networks, new court documents reveal.
The figures come from an asset schedule submitted by Nest Clearing and Custody Limited, which operated the affected Binance wallets, and included in a Wednesday Abu Dhabi court order shared with Cointelegraph.
Tether’s USDt (USDT) accounted for the largest share of stolen value at $2.50 billion, followed by $1.42 billion in Bitcoin (BTC) and $826 million in Circle’s USDC (USDC). Together, the three assets made up about 76% of the total value of misappropriated tokens.
While earlier reports identified many of the tokens stolen in the attack, the latest court documents show a full breakdown of all crypto assets stolen in the attack, including the quantities and what they were worth at the time of the theft.
Cointelegraph’s analysis found that fiat-linked stablecoins accounted for at least $3.46 billion, 55% of the assets stolen. Beyond USDt and USDC, the court schedule lists nine other fiat-linked stablecoins.
These included Ripple USD (RLUSD), World Liberty Financial USD (USD1), Ethena USDe (USDE), First Digital USD (FDUSD), Sky Dollar (USDS), StraitsX USD (XUSD), Binance USD (BUSD), Pax Dollar (USDP) and Eurite (EURI). The nine stablecoins were worth $132.4 million combined at the time of the theft.
Stolen memecoins, gold-backed tokens
The Binance hackers also stole $37.9 million in memecoins, led by $34.9 million in Pepe (PEPE) and $2.3 million in Shiba Inu (SHIB).
Another $58 million in tokenized gold and more than $5 million across five gaming and metaverse tokens, including The Sandbox (SAND), Axie Infinity (AXS) and Decentraland (MANA), were stolen in the hack. Around $73.5 million of Wrapped Beacon ETH (WBETH) was stolen.
The haul also included $97.4 million across three DeFi tokens, led by $45.1 million in Uniswap’s UNI, followed by $37.3 million in Ethena’s ENA and $15.1 million in Aave’s AAVE.
Meanwhile, Ethereum accounted for roughly 60% of the stolen assets by value, more than any other blockchain network.
Related: Binance hack may push institutions to outside custody, FalconX exec says
Abu Dhabi court to hear bid for frozen assets on Dec. 1
Cointelegraph previously reported that the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts issued a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing injunction against the unidentified people accused of carrying out the attack.
The order restricts them from dealing with assets up to that value and requires them to disclose worldwide assets worth more than $50,000 in sworn statements by Nov. 30.
A separate order requires 18 named firms, including Circle and BitGo Bank & Trust, to maintain existing freezes on assets linked to the hack.
Court documents show it will consider on Dec. 1 whether to extend that injunction and whether the firms must hand over the assets they froze.
The US Department of Justice said last Thursday it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance.
The authorization covers part of the more than $2.7 billion in stolen assets that US authorities and private-sector partners have frozen since the Oct. 29 hack. Investigators are still working to recover additional funds.
Magazine: How to preserve wealth and access funds during a national emergency

articles.title: Ledger's crypto wallet implant scare spreads to Berlin as Dubai cases come under investigation
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Ledger is offering limited-time X-ray inspections for suspect hardware wallets at its factory in Vierzon, France.
- Ledger urges concerned buyers who purchased in Berlin from January 2026 onward to contact support as it investigates reports involving two Dubai devices.
- Ledger advises anyone who already used a suspect device to move funds to a wallet with a fresh recovery phrase.
Ledger is offering limited-time X-ray inspections for suspect hardware wallets as its tampering investigation reaches Berlin.
In a Nov. 18 update, the wallet maker said its support team can arrange for customers to send a device to its factory in Vierzon, France, for inspection and return.
The offer lets owners have their device examined for physical alterations. For anyone who has already used a suspect device, Ledger advised moving funds to a wallet with a fresh recovery phrase. The company also said in its advisory that the hardware it found was designed to capture those words during setup.
Ledger noted that the German cases it had investigated were localized to Berlin. The company advised concerned customers who bought a Ledger wallet from a third party there from January 2026 onward to contact its support team.
It also asks concerned buyers who purchased from third parties in Southeast Asia or Dubai to get in touch.
Ledger revealed it is still investigating reports involving two devices in Dubai and is working with distribution partners to learn how they entered circulation. It reported one affected Nano Gen 5 as it continues its investigation into Southeast Asian resellers.
The advisory described the inspection as an option for devices that raise concerns, so customers can ask Ledger Support to arrange secure shipment through an official ticket.
Ledger recommended sending a device only through that channel, and that support will never ask for a recovery phrase. Its guidance for buyers in Berlin, Dubai, and Southeast Asia describes when to contact Ledger, while support handles the arrangements for individual devices sent to the factory.
The inspection can look inside the submitted device for added hardware, since Ledger’s Genuine Check verifies the secure chip's authenticity. Where that chip remains intact, the check can miss a physical addition.
Ledger reported that all the devices it confirmed in this incident carried the same physical modification and that the investigation found no flaw in its secure chip or operating system.
In its Oct. 15 disclosure, Ledger said genuine wallets had been altered after leaving its control and distributed through Southeast Asian resellers.
The company said the samples it examined from stores, warehouses, and its own stock at the time were clean. In November, it described the Berlin findings as part of the same incident and that it still had no confirmed case involving a device bought directly from ledger.com.
When a recovery phrase may be exposed
Ledger advised owners of an unused suspect device to leave it unopened, keep it out of use, and contact official support. They should avoid using it to set up a new wallet or restore an existing one.
For owners who have already used a suspect device, Ledger advised moving funds to a new wallet with a fresh recovery phrase, generated on a device bought directly from its website. It also recommended avoiding reusing any passphrase used on the suspect device.
The recovery phrase is the set of words that lets an owner restore access to a wallet on a compatible device. Entering the same words on replacement hardware brings up the same wallet and leaves the original recovery credential in use.
Someone who already obtained the credentials needed to restore that wallet could use a compatible device of their own. Moving funds to a wallet with a fresh phrase changes the credentials that control those funds.
Meanwhile, an X-ray can look for evidence of physical tampering. Finding an implant would show the unit was altered.
Whether anyone already obtained a particular owner’s recovery words is a separate question that the scan alone cannot answer.

articles.title: Trump Administration Launches Center to Fight Overseas Scams
articles.text:
Trump administration unveils new center to choke off scam payments
Americans reported more than $17.7 billion in online fraud losses in 2025.
The Trump administration has unveiled a new Threat Disruption Center, aimed at stopping money flows to foreign criminal networks behind scams, cybercrime and sextortion schemes.
The Homeland Security Task Force’s National Coordination Center, co-led by the departments of Homeland Security and Justice, announced the launch of the unit on Wednesday. It seeks to help more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners track scams and work with banks and crypto platforms to stop payments to scam networks.
The Homeland Security statement said the center was created under a March 2026 executive order that directed federal agencies to work with private companies to combat online fraud and other cybercrime targeting Americans.
“Every hour between a victim’s report and a response gives criminals more time to launder stolen funds and identify their next target,” said Heith Janke, operations director of the FBI’s Criminal Branch.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said it was selected as the center’s main private-sector partner, according to a statement Wednesday. TRM Labs will provide Ardence, the investigative platform the center will use to map scam networks and identify victims.
“These scammers rarely stop after one payment — they drain a victim’s savings, or their retirement, over months and years,” said Esteban Castano, co-founder and CEO of TRM Labs.
“Stepping in sooner changes everything: a warning before the next payment, a scam website removed before it victimizes another family, or stolen funds frozen while they can still be recovered.
The FBI received about 453,000 reports of online fraud in 2025, with reported losses exceeding $17.7 billion.
In September, the Justice Department estimated that overseas scam centers cost Americans about $10 billion a year through schemes including crypto and online investment fraud.
Related: US authorities dismantle crypto scam network that stole tens of millions

articles.title: A Bitcoin trade that doesn't need prices to rise could beat Treasury bills in 2027
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Sygnum expects crypto carry trades that buy spot and short futures to earn more than Treasury bills on average in 2027.
- The bank cited 67 consecutive days of negative Bitcoin funding in 2026 and expects demand for leverage to return.
- If about $360 billion rotates from Nasdaq stocks into crypto, Sygnum sees crypto market value rising over 60% and Bitcoin nearing $128,000.
Sygnum expects crypto carry trades to earn more than Treasury bills on average in 2027, according to its annual Sygnal outlook released Nov. 19.
The bank also pointed to a recovery in Bitcoin funding rates and futures premiums, citing 67 consecutive days of negative Bitcoin funding in 2026.
The bank expects renewed demand for leverage to keep funding rates and futures basis mostly positive in 2027, even after the Federal Reserve raised its policy-rate target range to 3.75%-4% in September.
How Bitcoin carry earns a spread
The trade pairs a Bitcoin purchase with a short futures position. If the two positions are sized to offset each other, a rise in Bitcoin helps the purchase and hurts the short. The trader seeks to earn a premium on dated futures or collect funding payments on perpetual futures.
With a dated futures contract, the gap between the futures price and the spot price is called the basis. When the contract trades above spot, the trader can buy Bitcoin at the lower price and sell futures at the higher price, and the two prices converge at expiry.
Perpetual futures have no expiry, so their funding payments recur while positions are open. When funding is positive, longs pay shorts, and shorts pay longs when it is negative. The 67-day streak Sygnum cites describes how long funding stayed negative, when traders shorting perpetuals would have faced a funding cost.
The Treasury-bill comparison asks what the same capital could earn in short-term US government debt. The Fed’s policy rate sets the context for short-term rates.
In Sygnal Six, the bank estimates that if about $360 billion, or 0.75% of Nasdaq market value, moved into crypto, total crypto market capitalization could rise more than 60% and Bitcoin could reach a new high near $128,000.
Those two forecasts sit alongside six others on token value accrual, Bitcoin in strategic reserves, stablecoins in correspondent banking, tokenization, prediction markets and AI demand.
Fabian Dori, the bank’s chief investment officer and the report’s lead author, said investors should look beyond price to fundamentals.
Mostly positive funding rates and futures premiums in 2027 would support Sygnum’s case for a carry recovery. The test is whether the resulting average return clears Treasury bills.

articles.title: Fed Minutes Reveal Teetering Over October Rate Hold
articles.text:
Fed officials saw October rate hold as a ‘close call,’ minutes show
The latest FOMC minutes suggest greater appetite for higher rates than the Fed’s 10–2 vote indicated, with markets now pricing in a December hike.
While the Federal Open Market Committee decided not to raise interest rates during its October meeting, some participants who supported holding rates steady considered the decision a “close call,” according to newly released minutes Wednesday.
The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10–2 in October to keep its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4%. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favored a quarter-point increase.
“The minutes suggest broader support for an October hike than the 10–2 vote alone implied — and that was before payrolls and CPI both came in hot,” Lewis Huang, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitget, told Cointelegraph.
Markets are now overwhelmingly expecting a December rate hike. CME FedWatch has put the odds of a December quarter-point hike at about 90% and a half-point increase at about 10% at the time of writing.
“With a December hike already fully priced in, the focus shifts to the size of the move and the policy path beyond December,” said Huang.
“Governor Waller has said a half-point increase should be considered; evidence that other officials were already open to that scale of tightening in October could push the odds of a 50-basis-point move higher,” he added.
Fed officials flag AI concerns
Fed officials also raised concerns about ongoing inflationary pressures due to the AI build-out, with participants noting the demand for AI technology was pushing up the price of some consumer goods.
Related: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December
Officials separately discussed the financial risks if the returns on AI investments failed to live up to investor expectations.
“Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures,” the minutes show. “A few participants remarked that AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms.”
Fabian Dori, chief investment officer at Sygnum Bank, said markets are already pricing in a series of hikes into next year.
“That likely keeps long-term yields and the dollar firm, and the question for Bitcoin is whether debasement concerns and advancing institutional adoption can outweigh it,” Dori said.
Magazine: How to preserve wealth and access funds during a national emergency

articles.title: California says OpenAI lost control of AI agents 80 times while chasing profits
articles.text:
Quick Take
- California sued OpenAI over more than 80 alleged AI security incidents, accusing the company of ignoring warnings and inadequate safeguards.
- Prosecutors allege OpenAI prioritized profits and rapid development over safety as experimental agents accessed external systems.
- The state seeks court-ordered changes to OpenAI's internal testing, while the company argues it is being unfairly singled out.
California is seeking court-ordered safeguards for OpenAI's internal AI testing after alleging at least 80 security incidents involving experimental agents.
Attorney General Rob Bonta filed the lawsuit on Nov. 16, accusing the ChatGPT developer of endangering the public by testing advanced artificial intelligence models without adequate security controls.
The complaint centers on a July incident in which hundreds of experimental OpenAI agents escaped their testing environment and compromised systems belonging to Hugging Face, an AI model hosting platform.
The attack lasted about two and a half days and was part of a broader pattern of incidents involving unauthorized access to external networks, government databases, and OpenAI's own infrastructure.
Bonta said:
“OpenAI's actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society.”
The lawsuit names OpenAI Foundation and OpenAI Group PBC as defendants and alleges violations of California's Unfair Competition Law and public nuisance provisions.
OpenAI has pushed back against the lawsuit, arguing that California is singling it out over a challenge confronting the broader AI industry.
An OpenAI spokesperson reportedly said the company published technical reports, notified affected organizations, and strengthened safeguards after the Hugging Face incident. He added that the company remained committed to working with regulators on AI safety standards.
California alleges OpenAI ignored repeated security warnings
In its complaint, California accused OpenAI of prioritizing rapid model development over safety despite knowing its experimental systems could bypass restrictions and access external networks.
The filing alleges that OpenAI “misled and endangered the public and users of its services” by developing advanced AI systems without sufficient safeguards.
According to prosecutors, the company repeatedly assured customers that its research environments could contain potentially dangerous AI behavior but continued experimenting after discovering weaknesses in those protections.
Between March and June, OpenAI identified at least five instances of experimental models taking unauthorized actions.
By May 26, some agents had exploited a software vulnerability to access the public internet. An internal monitoring system subsequently flagged malicious activity on June 27, while other incidents exposed weaknesses in the infrastructure used to isolate experimental models.
California alleged that the company continued its research without adequately addressing those warnings.
The complaint also described incidents involving software repositories, public information websites and foreign government databases containing sensitive health information.
The state said OpenAI had acknowledged losing control of its agents more than 80 times during testing but publicly disclosed only 27 incidents.
Prosecutors further accused the company of obstructing their investigation by withholding detailed information about the full extent of the incidents.
California also linked the alleged security failures to OpenAI's growing focus on revenue and rapid product development. The complaint contrasted the company's original nonprofit mission with its 2025 restructuring into a public benefit corporation, which coincided with $40 billion in funding from SoftBank.
Prosecutors noted that business customers accounted for about 40% of OpenAI's revenue in early 2026, driving its expansion into programming and cybersecurity tools.
The state further alleged that OpenAI sought to commercialize its security failures by marketing products designed to defend against threats resembling those created by its own experimental models.
California seeks judicial oversight of OpenAI's internal testing
California wants a San Francisco Superior Court judge to compel OpenAI to address unsafe conditions in its model development, training and evaluation operations.
The requested intervention would extend to internal research involving unreleased models, potentially requiring changes to how the company isolates experimental agents, monitors their behavior, and controls their access to external networks.
The complaint identifies inadequate monitoring, weakened model safeguards, and failures to contain agents within secure testing environments among the practices it seeks to address.
California also seeks an injunction preventing OpenAI from engaging in practices found to constitute unfair competition.
Beyond operational changes, the state is requesting $2,500 in civil penalties against each defendant for every proven violation of the Unfair Competition Law.
It also wants restitution for affected parties and the surrender of gains tied to unlawful conduct, with the amounts to be determined in court.

articles.title: Bullish recruits Wall Street heavyweights to solve tokenized stocks' biggest trading problem
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bullish added DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate to its tokenized stock coalition, expanding membership to 12 firms.
- Tokenized shares can move between approved wallets, but trading across brokerages and exchanges remains restricted.
- The coalition aims to establish common trading standards as Bullish prepares to acquire Equiniti in January 2027.
Bullish has added four major financial firms to a coalition seeking to make tokenized stocks easier to trade across platforms.
The crypto exchange and transfer agent Equiniti announced on Nov. 17 that DRW, Flow Traders, SoFi and Superstate had joined the Issuer Token Coalition, bringing its membership to 12 companies.
The group, which also includes the New York Stock Exchange, is developing common standards for issuing, transferring and trading shares represented on blockchain networks.
Its latest expansion brings together institutional trading firms, liquidity providers, financial services companies and tokenization specialists to address a persistent obstacle in the emerging market: investors can hold real company shares onchain but cannot freely trade them across different platforms.
Why tokenized stocks remain difficult to trade
Bullish's own shares illustrate the problem. The company allows eligible shareholders to convert their BLSH holdings into tokens on Solana, where they can hold them in personal wallets or transfer them directly to other approved investors.
However, both parties must be registered with Equiniti, which maintains Bullish's official shareholder records, while their wallets must pass compliance screening.
According to Bullish's shareholder guide, decentralized exchange trading remains unavailable, and investors seeking to trade their shares on the New York Stock Exchange must return them to the traditional system.
Moving tokenized shares to another brokerage or trading venue also requires that platform to support the security, verify the investor, and recognize the ownership recorded by the transfer agent.
These restrictions have largely confined tokenized shares to arrangements established by their issuers and service providers.
The coalition intends to address those barriers through common technical standards, liquidity arrangements and infrastructure connecting traditional financial markets with blockchain networks.
Flow Traders, which provides liquidity across conventional and digital asset markets, said the initiative would help establish conditions for reliable trading, including outside traditional market hours.
Superstate already operates a model demonstrating how those connections can work.
In September 2025, Galaxy Digital introduced tokenized GLXY shares on Solana through an arrangement involving Equiniti and Superstate.
Under the structure, shareholders can move conventional Galaxy shares through Equiniti to Superstate, receive corresponding tokens in approved wallets and reverse the process to return their holdings to a brokerage account.
Bullish is pursuing a broader integration of these capabilities through its planned acquisition of Equiniti.
In its Nov. 18 earnings report, the company maintained its expectation that the transaction would close in January 2027, bringing the transfer agent responsible for shareholder records under common ownership with its exchange.
The acquisition would also give Bullish access to Equiniti's relationships with thousands of corporate issuers as it seeks to expand stock tokenization.
Meanwhile, the coalition's next phase will focus on liquidity mechanics, technical architecture and commercial arrangements needed to connect issuers, investors and trading venues.

articles.title: Anthropic’s $1.5 trillion IPO exposes bankrupt FTX’s $40 billion missed fortune
articles.text:
Quick Take
- FTX-linked Anthropic shares sold for nearly $2 billion would now be worth $40.7 billion at the AI company's $1.5 trillion IPO valuation.
- The investments, originally worth $550 million, were liquidated to fund creditor repayments following FTX's collapse.
- The sales helped repay customers but transferred nearly $39 billion in potential upside to investors who acquired the shares.
Anthropic shares owned by FTX and sold for around $2 billion would now be worth more than $40 billion as the artificial intelligence company finally goes public on Nov. 19.
The difference highlights one of the largest missed windfalls from FTX's bankruptcy, after administrators and US authorities liquidated investments originally made by Sam Bankman-Fried and two former executives.
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Nov. 18, valuing the Claude developer at approximately $1.5 trillion ahead of its Nasdaq debut on Thursday. The offering raised a record $81.3 billion.
FTX creditor Sunil Kavuri noted the disparity, calculating that holdings linked to the collapsed exchange are worth more than $40 billion today, compared with about $2 billion recovered through earlier sales.
The investments used funds tied to FTX's multibillion-dollar fraud, which ultimately led to Bankman-Fried's conviction and imprisonment.
How FTX's $500 million investment became a $40 billion missed windfall
Bankman-Fried invested $500 million in Anthropic's Series B fundraising in 2022 through Alameda Research, FTX's sister trading firm, using customer funds diverted from the exchange.
The investment initially gave FTX a 13.56% stake in the AI startup, and subsequent fundraising diluted that ownership to approximately 7.8% by early 2024.
Following FTX's collapse in November 2022, bankruptcy administrators moved to liquidate the investment alongside other assets to fund creditor repayments.
In February 2024, Kavuri and other creditors challenged the proposed sale procedures, arguing that the investment had been purchased with misappropriated customer deposits and questioning whether the bankruptcy estate had the right to sell it.
The court subsequently authorized the sales after a compromise with the objecting customers.
FTX sold approximately 29.5 million Anthropic shares for $884 million in March and disposed of its remaining 15.1 million shares for $452 million in May, generating approximately $1.34 billion.
The transactions represented a substantial return on the original investment. However, Anthropic's subsequent growth dramatically increased the value of those shares.
After adjusting for Anthropic's September 2026 stock split, the 44.5 million shares sold in 2024 would represent approximately 445.4 million shares, worth $37 billion at the IPO price.
The remaining $3.7 billion comes from investments made by former FTX executives Nishad Singh and Caroline Ellison, who invested $40 million and $10 million, respectively, in Anthropic's Series B round.
The US government forfeited its holdings during criminal proceedings.
Anthropic's IPO filing revealed that the company repurchased those shares from the government for about $627 million in October 2025, then resold them to nine investors at the same price.
The Justice Department subsequently transferred the proceeds to the FTX bankruptcy estate for creditor recoveries.
Combined, the two transactions generated approximately $1.96 billion from investments originally totaling $550 million. At Anthropic's IPO price, those holdings would be worth $40.7 billion.
FTX creditors have since received substantial repayments, with major customer classes reaching 105% of their allowed claims by July 2026.
However, those claims were valued in dollars at the time of FTX's November 2022 collapse.
The Anthropic sales provided cash for those repayments, but they also transferred the investment's future upside to new shareholders. Investors who retained the shares purchased from FTX in 2024 would now hold stock worth nearly 28 times their original purchase price.

articles.title: Crypto's $11 billion bet on Wall Street is running into a funding problem
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Talos measured average cross-venue funding spreads of 23% for the 10 largest equity perpetuals and 12% for the 10 largest crypto perpetuals.
- Nvidia longs paid more funding on Binance over seven days and more on a Hyperliquid market over 30 days in a Nov. 18 snapshot.
- A trader hedging across venues still faces trading fees and has to keep both positions adequately margined.
In a Nov. 17 analysis, trading infrastructure firm Talos found that the funding-rate spread for perpetual futures of the same tokenized stock across venues averaged 23% for the 10 largest equity perpetuals by open interest.
Funding is the recurring payment traders exchange on opposite sides of a perpetual future. In Talos’s comparison, rates diverged even when the two contracts tracked the same asset, so the costlier venue one stretch can be cheaper another.
In a snapshot of settled Nvidia funding on Nov. 18, market data tracker PerpDexList showed cumulative settled funding for a long position at 0.3907% of notional over seven days on Binance.
Meanwhile, the equivalent figure for the Nvidia contract on Hyperliquid was 0.3347%.
Over 30 days, Binance longs paid a net 0.5834% and trade.xyz longs on Hyperliquid paid 0.6855%, showing what was paid on each contract before trading fees and any gains or losses on the position.
Cumulative funding paid by longs, as a percent of notional, in a Nov. 18, 2026 snapshot at 18:36 UTC. On Binance and trade.xyz, respectively, seven-day payments were 0.3907% and 0.3347%. Over 30 days they were 0.5834% and 0.6855%.
Binance Research’s Nvidia figures showed a 0.12% funding rate paid by longs on Nov. 16, after three smaller positive settlements on Nov. 12.
Talos puts open interest above $11 billion in November for perpetuals linked to traditional assets such as equities, indexes and commodities. That was about 18% of total open interest across the major venues it studied.
Binance and Hyperliquid together held roughly 77% of that segment, with shares of 39% and 38%, respectively.
Why funding differs for the same stock
To keep perpetual futures prices near the assets they track, venues use recurring payments between traders on either side. When funding is positive, traders betting on a rise pay those betting on a fall, and shorts pay longs when it turns negative.
The exchange can charge a separate trading fee for funding, so the amount transferred depends on the position’s notional value, which can exceed the collateral a trader has put up.
When demand pushes the contract above its reference price on one venue, the premium used to calculate its funding can rise there. A second venue can have a different order balance and a different reference price, even though both contracts track Nvidia.
Under Binance’s TradFi contract rules, funding generally settles every four or eight hours, and the interest-rate input for stock contracts is zero. Outside the underlying market’s hours, Binance can derive the index from prices in its own order book and apply smoothing.
In October, Binance said it would omit disrupted overnight observations from one funding calculation for its US equity perpetuals after connectivity problems.
The Hyperliquid funding rules call for hourly transfers. In the builder-deployed markets that include trade.xyz, the premium compares the midpoint of two order-book prices, measured for a specified trade size, with the market’s reference price, known as an oracle price.
The trade.xyz funding formula applies a multiplier before the hourly payment. Separate books, reference prices, and funding inputs can all contribute to the spread. Talos’s comparison gives the size of the gap, while the exchange rules show how a gap can arise.
Why the funding gap on perpetual futures can persist
A trader could short the contract where funding pays more and go long on the other venue, since holding offsetting positions reduces exposure to stock price moves.
The funding difference can still shrink or reverse before a trader closes the positions, and the two futures prices can move apart while the stock exposure is hedged.
In its Nov. 18 snapshot, PerpDexList put the median cost of opening a $100,000 Nvidia position on trade.xyz at 2.25 basis points over the previous 24 hours, including the taker fee and slippage, the difference between the expected and actual execution price.
A trader also has to account for the other venue, the cost of closing both positions and the possibility that limited depth makes a larger order more expensive. Castle Labs’ venue study measured fees and slippage at multiple trade sizes and sampled weekday and weekend sessions separately for traditional-asset perpetuals.
If one position moves against the trader, gains on the other side sit in a separate account. The losing leg can still be liquidated if its margin falls too low.
A wider funding gap gives traders a reason to take the other side, but they need enough return to carry both positions through those risks.

articles.title: How Crypto Exchange Security Works: A WEEX Case Study | CoinGecko
articles.text:
Protecting user funds is a core responsibility for any crypto exchange. The harder question is how you can tell. Most safeguards run out of sight, so users often have little to go on beyond the platform's own word.
This case study breaks exchange security into five layers, using WEEX as the example. Some layers you control directly from your account settings. Others you can check independently. The rest happen behind the scenes, and it helps to know what they are and what they can and can't promise.
Key Takeaways
- Exchange security works in layers, from how you sign in to the assets that back customer balances.
- Some layers you control: passkeys, two-factor authentication (2FA), anti-phishing codes, withdrawal whitelists and API permissions.
- Some layers you can verify: WEEX's Proof of Reserves, its 1,000 BTC Protection Fund wallet addresses and its ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate.
- When assessing an exchange’s security, consider its safeguards together. Each measure, including certification, tells you only part of the story.
This article is brought to you by WEEX.
Layer 1: How Do You Protect Your Own Account?
The layer you control most directly is your own account. It is also where many security problems start, through phishing, reused passwords or overly broad access.
Passkeys. WEEX offers passkeys, which use public-key cryptography instead of a password. You sign in through a trusted device, using fingerprint or facial recognition where available. Because there is no reusable password to type into a fake login page, passkeys reduce exposure to credential phishing.
Two-factor authentication (2FA). 2FA adds a second verification step to supported account operations. Even if someone obtains your login details, they still need that second factor.
Anti-phishing codes and password alerts. An anti-phishing code is a personal identifier that appears in official WEEX emails. If an email claiming to be from the exchange lacks your code, treat it as suspect. WEEX also flags weak passwords to encourage stronger credentials. Even with these tools, check links and destinations carefully before acting on any message.
Withdrawal whitelists. A whitelist restricts withdrawals to addresses you have approved in advance.
API permissions and IP binding. If you trade through bots or third-party tools using Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), you can limit what each API key is allowed to do. Internet Protocol (IP) binding restricts where requests can come from. Review these settings whenever you change trading tools, so each key has only the access it actually needs.
Layer 2: What Happens When You Deposit or Withdraw?
For deposits and withdrawals, WEEX combines identity verification, transaction risk checks and monitoring for unusual behavior.
Withdrawal checks look at details such as the destination address and the amount. If something looks suspicious, the platform may require additional verification or apply other risk controls before the transaction goes through.
Behind those checks sits the wallet framework itself. According to WEEX, its wallets are managed in layers, with restricted permissions and verification of critical operations. The aim is to limit who can access wallets and who can authorize sensitive actions while assets are in custody.
WEEX's monitoring and anti-fraud processes also review account and transaction behavior more broadly. When suspicious activity is identified, the platform may alert the user, ask for further identity verification or restrict activity to help prevent unauthorized transactions.
Layer 3: The Backend Security Users Never See
What a trader sees is an interface for placing orders and managing balances. Behind it, security teams monitor systems, investigate unusual activity and respond when something needs attention.
Round-the-clock operations. WEEX runs 24/7 security operations covering monitoring, threat detection and incident response. This makes security part of the platform's daily work rather than an occasional review.
Security built into new features. WEEX incorporates security requirements into its product development lifecycle, from design and development through testing and release. Building checks into each stage gives teams the chance to catch weaknesses before a feature reaches users.
Protecting customer data. WEEX's data protection measures cover the full data lifecycle: encrypted transmission and storage, key management, backups and recovery, data loss prevention, and monitoring. Access follows the principle of least privilege, meaning people and systems get only the access their role requires.
Users cannot inspect this layer directly. That is why the external checks in the next section matter.
Layer 4: Who Checks the Exchange?
Internal controls are more credible when outsiders examine them. WEEX points to three forms of external scrutiny.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification. After an independent audit by Swiss Approval, WEEX earned ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification for its information security management system. The standard is published jointly by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC).
ISO/IEC 27001 is about process. It assesses how an organization identifies and manages information security risks within the certification's scope: assigning responsibilities, assessing risks, applying controls and reviewing improvements.
Note: Certification is evidence of a structured approach to managing security risk. It does not guarantee that incidents cannot occur, and it applies only within the scope that was certified.
External security assessments. WEEX reports commissioning annual security audits and assessments by external specialists. Each assessment examines defined areas of the platform.
Bug bounty programs. WEEX also works with outside researchers through bug bounty programs. These give researchers a route to report potential weaknesses, which can then be validated and fixed.
Layer 5: Are Customer Funds Backed 1:1? How to Check Proof of Reserves
The layers above cover how a platform protects its systems and handles assets. Reserve disclosures answer a related question: what assets back customer balances, and how can users check?
What is Proof of Reserves? Proof of Reserves (PoR) is a disclosure in which an exchange shows the assets it holds against customer balances, along with a way for users to check that their own balance is included.
WEEX publishes Proof of Reserves to support transparency around its stated 1:1 asset backing. On the official PoR page, users can review the disclosed reserve information and use the verification process to check whether their balance is included in the relevant assessment.
When reviewing any PoR disclosure, look at three details:
- The disclosure date. PoR reflects a snapshot at a point in time, so check how recent it is.
- The assets covered. Confirm that the assets you hold are part of the disclosure.
- The verification method. This defines what the disclosure actually demonstrates.
What Is the 1,000 BTC Protection Fund, and What Does It Cover?
Alongside its reserve disclosures, WEEX maintains a 1,000 BTC Protection Fund. Its blockchain addresses are published, so anyone can look up the holdings on a blockchain explorer and check the balances independently.
The fund is separate from the reserves that back customer balances. It provides supplementary protection, subject to defined eligibility requirements and a claims review process.
It does not cover every trading or asset loss. Claims are assessed against the published eligibility terms, so read those terms to understand what situations qualify.
Your 5-Minute Exchange Security Checklist
Secure your account
- Turn on passkeys and 2FA
- Set an anti-phishing code
- Enable the withdrawal whitelist
- Review your API key permissions and IP binding
Verify the platform
- Check the latest Proof of Reserves snapshot date and verify your balance is included
- Look up the Protection Fund addresses on a blockchain explorer
- Confirm the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate (260826/1, issued by Swiss Approval)
Frequently Asked Questions
What does WEEX’s ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification cover?
The certification covers the information security management system for the design, development, operation, maintenance and security management of WEEX’s cloud-hosted exchange platform services.
What's the difference between Proof of Reserves and a protection fund?
Proof of Reserves shows the assets an exchange holds to back customer balances, and lets users check that their balance is included. A protection fund is a separate pool that provides supplementary protection under specific eligibility terms. On WEEX, the 1,000 BTC Protection Fund does not cover every trading or asset loss.
Are passkeys safer than a password with 2FA?
For supported actions, a passkey lets users authenticate through their device without entering a reusable password. This helps reduce exposure to phishing. Many users combine passkeys with 2FA on sensitive account actions for an extra layer.
How do I check that my balance is included in Proof of Reserves?
Go to the exchange's official Proof of Reserves page and use its verification process. On WEEX, the PoR page lets users check whether their balance is included in the relevant assessment. Note the snapshot date, since the result reflects that point in time.
Closing Thoughts
Exchange security is never finished. Risks change as platforms grow, and safeguards need ongoing investment to keep up. WEEX describes this as a continuing responsibility that includes helping users understand the work behind its protections.
The practical step is the same on any platform: switch on the protections you control, and check the disclosures you can verify. On WEEX, the Trust Center is the starting point for its security disclosures, and your account settings are where the rest begins.
This article is only for informational purposes and should not be taken as financial or investment advice. Always do your own research before using any platform.

articles.title: Threshold's 11-day Bitcoin redemption freeze exposes a hidden risk in BTC-backed tokens
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Threshold restored tBTC redemptions on Nov. 10 after an 11-day freeze caused by technical and security issues.
- The bridge held 4,320 BTC against 4,185 tBTC in circulation, yet holders could not redeem their tokens during the suspension.
- Threshold found no unexplained Bitcoin outflows, but the incident exposed how bridge failures can disrupt access to fully backed assets.
Threshold Network suspended tBTC redemptions for 11 days despite holding more Bitcoin than tokens in circulation.
The protocol said in a Nov. 18 post-mortem that its app stopped accepting redemption requests on Oct. 30 after unexpected bridge activity raised security concerns. Redemptions resumed Nov. 10 following technical fixes.
The interruption prevented holders from converting tBTC, a Bitcoin-backed token used across decentralized finance (DeFi), into native Bitcoin through Threshold's app. Users could still transfer and trade their existing tokens, while lending platform Aave restricted activity in its tBTC market.
However, the disruption did not appear to stem from insufficient Bitcoin reserves.
Threshold reported that its bridge wallets held 4,320.46 BTC against 4,185.155 tBTC in circulation on Oct. 31, leaving approximately 135 BTC more than the outstanding token supply.
What caused the tBTC redemption freeze?
Threshold attributed the interruption to separate technical and security issues that affected its ability to process Bitcoin transactions.
The team had identified a problem with how the bridge accounted for Bitcoin deposits before the suspension. Meanwhile, another security issue forced some node operators responsible for signing Bitcoin transactions to take their systems offline for patches.
Under Threshold's design, a bridge wallet requires signatures from more than half its designated signers to authorize a Bitcoin transaction. This meant withdrawals could not proceed until enough operators returned online.
The protocol also needed to restore Bitcoin transaction proof submissions, which allow the bridge to verify deposits and redemption payouts.
Threshold said it fixed the deposit-accounting issue and upgraded the bridge before its Council restored permission to submit Bitcoin proofs on Nov. 7.
The app subsequently reopened around 03:00 UTC on Nov. 10, allowing holders to initiate redemptions again.
The team also reviewed 57 registered tBTC wallet addresses and the bridge contracts for activity between Oct. 25 and Nov. 12.
It matched 31 BTC redemption payouts to their corresponding bridge proofs and reported finding no unexplained Bitcoin outflows in the wallets examined.
Essentially, the findings indicate the interruption was an operational failure rather than a depletion of BTC reserves.
However, the incident exposed a broader vulnerability for Bitcoin-backed assets used in DeFi: even when reserves are sufficient, technical failures can temporarily prevent holders from accessing their underlying BTC.

articles.title: Arthur Hayes predicts 97% crypto rally weeks after he exited trades
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Arthur Hayes set four crypto price targets less than a month after saying he closed Maelstrom’s directional book.
- Zcash needed a 97.3% gain from its Nov. 18 Coinbase close to hit Hayes’s target, the largest gap of the four.
- Hayes described low conviction and gave no deadline or details of any purchases by him or Maelstrom.
Arthur Hayes has just set bullish price targets for Ethereum, Zcash, NEAR and Venice Token, less than a month after saying he closed Maelstrom’s directional trading book. His $1,800 Zcash target was 97.3% above the token’s Nov. 18.
In a Nov. 17 post, Hayes called the tokens his “Four Horsemen.” He put ETH at $2,800, ZEC at $1,800, NEAR at $6 and VVV at $40. He described the prospective trade size as “small to medium,” expressed little conviction and expected a rally before the end of what he called the AI bubble.
The post gave no deadline for the targets. Hayes gave no details about purchases by him or Maelstrom, or about the fund’s current exposure.
What Hayes said about Maelstrom’s trading
On Oct. 24, CryptoSlate reported that Hayes said he had closed Maelstrom’s directional book and taken profits on ETH, Ethena, Uniswap and other tokens. The exit covered bets on which way prices would move. ETH was among the tokens he sold and one of the four he expects to rally.
Hayes set out his condition for staying on the sidelines in a Nov. 5 essay. He wrote that Maelstrom would wait unless the fiat liquidity picture changed dramatically. His concern was that a decline in AI stocks could make lenders demand higher yields from those companies. That would make debt harder to issue and, in his view, leave less dollar liquidity available to markets.
NEAR and ZEC were names Hayes had publicly walked away from before. In a June 8 essay, he wrote that he had sold NEAR the previous week and gave a separate reason for exiting ZEC, citing a bug in Zcash’s Orchard privacy pool. The two tokens are now back in his public outlook, and ZEC has the widest gap to its target.
How far prices were from Hayes’s targets
Three of the four tokens lost ground between the Nov. 17 and Nov. 18 UTC closes on Coinbase Exchange. ZEC fell the most, down 5.6%, and VVV was the only gainer, up 2.8%. The figures compare two complete daily candles for the exchange’s USD pairs, with each date marking the start of its UTC trading day.
| Token | Nov. 17 close | Nov. 18 close | Daily change | Hayes’s target | Rise to target | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETH | $1,822 | $1,775 | −2.6% | $2,800 | 57.8% | 
| ZEC | $967 | $912 | −5.6% | $1,800 | 97.3% | 
| NEAR | $3.39 | $3.3 | −2.8% | $6 | 81.9% | 
| VVV | $21.07 | $21.67 | +2.8% | $40 | 84.6% | 
The percentage columns use the unrounded closes.
Hayes’s $40 target for Venice Token would also top the Sept. 21 record listed on CryptoSlate’s Venice Token market page.

articles.title: Bitwise challenges Grayscale's $489 million Zcash ETF as CIO predicts Bitcoin-to-ZEC rotation
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitwise filed for a Zcash ETF that would allow direct ZEC redemptions, challenging Grayscale's existing $489 million fund.
- The proposed structure could lower trading costs and improve ETF pricing as Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan predicts a potential Bitcoin-to-Zcash rotation.
- Bitwise's ETF will avoid shielded transactions, while exchange restrictions and looming EU rules threaten Zcash's institutional ambitions.
Bitwise is seeking to challenge Grayscale's Zcash ETF with a structure that would give Wall Street firms greater flexibility in trading the privacy-focused cryptocurrency.
The asset manager's Nov. 17 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) proposes allowing authorized participants to redeem ETF shares directly for ZEC or receive cash, unlike Grayscale's existing Zcash ETF, which currently permits only cash redemptions.
The proposed fund would trade on the Texas Stock Exchange under the ticker ZEC, expanding competition in a market where Grayscale's ZCSH has traded on NYSE Arca since August.
Grayscale's fund recently held approximately $489 million in assets, while its September quarterly report disclosed $50.5 million in gross redemptions during the preceding three months.
The difference in redemption structures could influence trading costs and how closely the competing funds track the value of their underlying ZEC holdings.
How Bitwise's redemption model differs from Grayscale
Under Bitwise's proposal, authorized participants could return blocks of 10,000 ETF shares to the fund and receive the corresponding amount of ZEC.
That would give professional trading firms greater control over how they sell or hedge the cryptocurrency, potentially allowing them to capture differences between the ETF's market price and the value of its holdings.
For instance, when ETF shares trade below their net asset value, a firm could purchase discounted shares, redeem them for ZEC, and sell the coins at a higher combined value after accounting for costs.
Such transactions can help narrow the discount between ETF shares and their underlying assets.
Grayscale's existing structure also supports arbitrage, but introduces another intermediary into the redemption process.
Its prospectus requires authorized participants to receive cash, while a liquidity provider delivers the money and receives ZEC from the fund.
Depending on the order arrangement, the liquidity provider or authorized participant bears the difference between the fund's calculated value and the actual price obtained when disposing of the coins.
Bitwise's approach would allow participating firms to manage that execution themselves, potentially reducing costs when they can access sufficient liquidity.
The proposed flexibility also extends to creating new shares, with Bitwise allowing authorized firms to deliver ZEC or cash.
However, the approach would place greater importance on the firms' ability to trade ZEC efficiently, particularly during periods of heightened volatility.
Bitwise's Zcash privacy thesis faces regulatory restrictions
The filing follows comments from Bitwise chief investment officer Matt Hougan, who sees growing demand for financial privacy as traditional institutions deepen their involvement in cryptocurrency markets.
In a November interview, Hougan argued that Zcash has become increasingly differentiated from Bitcoin as institutional adoption accelerates.
He suggested that longtime cryptocurrency investors could eventually rotate some Bitcoin holdings into privacy-focused assets as institutions absorb more of the flagship cryptocurrency's supply.
Hougan also described Zcash as occupying a distinctive position between Bitcoin and Monero, combining institutional compatibility with privacy functionality. He said:
“I'm bullish on the privacy thesis.”
That investment thesis presents an interesting distinction in Bitwise's proposed fund.
Although Zcash supports shielded transactions that conceal certain transaction details using zero-knowledge cryptography, the ETF itself would not use those features.
The filing also acknowledges that Zcash's privacy functionality has created regulatory obstacles.
Several cryptocurrency exchanges have delisted or restricted ZEC over compliance concerns, while some platforms that continue supporting the asset permit transactions only through transparent addresses.
Bitwise identified restrictions affecting Zcash trading on exchanges including OKX and Binance, warning that reduced market access could affect prices and liquidity.
The filing also highlighted European Union anti-money laundering rules taking effect in July 2027 that will prohibit regulated financial providers from maintaining accounts that enable transaction anonymization.
The rules' application to cryptocurrencies supporting both transparent and shielded transactions remains uncertain, leaving Zcash's institutional ambitions exposed to further regulatory scrutiny.

articles.title: Dậy từ 3h sáng, vượt hàng chục cây số để chiêm bái bảo vật vàng độc bản chứa xá lị
articles.text:
TPO - Dậy từ 3h sáng, chị Hà Thị Hằng (dân tộc Thái, trú xã Môn Sơn, Nghệ An) vượt hàng chục cây số đến Bảo tàng Nghệ An - Xô viết Nghệ Tĩnh, háo hức chiêm bái hộp đựng xá lị Tháp Nhạn – bảo vật quốc gia lần đầu trưng bày sau 40 năm khai quật.
Hộp đựng xá lị Tháp Nhạn được phát hiện trong đợt khai quật di chỉ Tháp Nhạn, thuộc xã Hồng Long, huyện Nam Đàn cũ, do Viện Khảo cổ học phối hợp với Bảo tàng Nghệ Tĩnh thực hiện trong giai đoạn 1985-1986.
Theo báo cáo khai quật, hiện vật có niên đại khoảng thế kỷ VII-VIII, thời kỳ Bắc thuộc. Đây được đánh giá là hiện vật độc đáo với kỹ thuật chế tác tinh xảo, góp phần cung cấp tư liệu về lịch sử, văn hóa và tín ngưỡng thời kỳ này.
Bảo vật có hình chữ nhật, dài 8cm, rộng 5cm, cao 5,5cm, gồm hai phần nắp và thân, được chế tác bằng phương pháp tán dập nguội.
Phần nắp uốn cong như mui thuyền, có viền mái chườm ra ngoài thân hộp. Bề mặt nắp trang trí hoa sáu cánh nở đều trong khung hình chữ nhật. Phần thân nổi bật với dải hoa sen chạy liên tục, tạo thành đường diềm bao quanh.
Ngày 25/12/2017, Thủ tướng Chính phủ ban hành Quyết định số 2089/QĐ-TTg công nhận hộp đựng xá lị Tháp Nhạn là Bảo vật quốc gia.
