articles.title: Anthropic's IPO puts AI's circular financing boom to the test | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Arriving at public markets today, Anthropic’s IPO is poised to raise billions for the company and its investors. But the biggest surprise may be just how much of that money will end up going to supplier-investors.
Amazon and Google, two of Anthropic’s largest infrastructure partners, hold stakes valued around a combined $307.9 billion at the company’s updated IPO price of $83 per share. Amazon, which invested $18 billion into the AI startup, would see its 14.7% stake hit upwards of $159 billion, while Google’s 13.7% stake is valued at nearly $149 billion, according to share ownership figures disclosed in Anthropic’s IPO prospectus.
A handful of other AI infrastructure providers are also positioned to benefit. Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC have joined Google in committing $26 billion to Anthropic at its IPO price in a private placement.
In total, Google has invested $12.3 billion into Anthropic since 2023, with another promised $30 billion dependent on Anthropic meeting certain performance milestones. And with the exception of TSMC, Anthropic has announced multibillion-dollar strategic partnerships with its other infrastructure supplier investors — including Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft, and Micron — that would see Anthropic purchasing their products.
This is the circular financing that has made some observers so skeptical of the AI boom. These companies are not just investors; they’re also Anthropic’s biggest suppliers. It might look like Amazon and Google are putting billions into Anthropic, but they get that money right back when Anthropic needs to train a model or serve Claude to users. From afar, it looks like unprecedented revenue growth for cloud companies and unprecedented fundraising from Anthropic — but it’s just the same money passing from one pocket to another.
Today’s IPO marks a critical change in that financing system, the moment it might just become self-sustaining. Those investments appear to have paid off, and are now liquid. Anthropic is still operating at a net loss of tens of billions of dollars each quarter — but it will no longer be suppliers and private investors footing the bill. Now, capital will come from a mix of public-market investors and corporate bonds, neither of which have the conflicts-of-interest that caused concerns before.
And critically, the company’s new bottom line looks pretty good.
Once it debuts, Anthropic is expected to have about $220 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, including proceeds from its IPO and the $26 billion private placement. Anthropic also has the ability to pay for future commitments in stock.
Joey Brookhart, who leads the Tokenomics team at SemiAnalysis, estimates that Anthropic needs roughly $280 billion in cumulative revenue over the next four years to pay for its compute bill, which Brookhart said is “achievable given where they will be next year from a revenue perspective.”
“The ownership stake is very worthwhile, and those companies no longer need any more support from [suppliers],” Brookhart told TechCrunch. “Amazon doesn’t need to prop them up anymore. The revenue is all coming from other customers.”
That doesn’t mean the server bills are going down, though. Anthropic has already committed to spend $900 billion, primarily for compute and infrastructure, according to a regulatory filing. Certain agreements have termination provisions, but Brookhart thinks the company is in a strong position to pay up.
On the other side, Anthropic generated $17 billion in third-quarter 2026 revenue, putting the company on pace for a $68 billion annualized rate for the year. If Anthropic continues to grow at its current trajectory, Brookhart believes it could easily cover the gap needed to fund its compute.
Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, agreed.
“By the time the IPO is done, Anthropic’s going to have more cash on hand than any company has ever had,” Luria told TechCrunch, noting that the firm raised around $141 billion in capital and will take home around $91.7 billion in net proceeds at $83 per share. “And they’re not burning cash. They’re just going to have a war chest.”
A public listing will make Anthropic a more credible borrower, making it easier to raise money outside of public markets, says Brookhart. That’s despite recent reports that creditors might not see Anthropic as “investment-grade” material.
Luria distinguished between Anthropic’s supplier investments and neoclouds like CoreWeave, which he sees as more purely supported by circular financing. “CoreWeave wouldn’t exist if Nvidia didn’t prop them up, and it probably won’t exist if Nvidia doesn’t bail them out,” Luria said.
Brookhart also pushed back on describing Anthropic’s financing as purely circular, saying it was still “additive to the ecosystem.”
For both analysts, the biggest risk to Anthropic is simply that it will lose the AI race. Right now, the company’s growth is fueled by its status at the frontier of generative AI — but if it’s overtaken by OpenAI, Google DeepMind, or even cheap open-weight models, that could change fast. As Luria put it: “If we’re all using other people’s models, then Anthropic’s not worth a trillion and a half dollars. It’s worth nothing.”
But regardless of who wins the frontier, compute suppliers will likely be just fine. Neither Brookhart nor Luria believe Anthropic’s growth is at risk, despite some arguments that cheaper tokens and more competition will directly affect the AI company’s bottom line.
“For Amazon and Google, the risk isn’t actually that high because in that scenario, we’re using other models,” Luria said. “I’m arguing we’re going to use a lot more AI. I don’t know if it’s all Anthropic’s AI…. That’s still going to come from a data center managed by Amazon, Google, and Microsoft.”

articles.title: DOJ accuses Russian national of spying on and harassing Palantir employees - Engadget
articles.text:
DOJ accuses Russian national of spying on and harassing Palantir employees
He allegedly took photos of their work laptops and even once followed a female employee for 30 miles.
A Russian national has been indicted for spying on and harassing the employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company, according to the Department of Justice. While the agency's announcement didn't name the specific company, Bloomberg reports that it was Palantir, and that the Russian national was told to do so over Ukraine's use of the company's software for wartime purposes.
Igor D'iu was reportedly recruited by the Russian government through Telegram, where he also received orders on what to do, the DOJ says. He traveled from Istanbul, Turkey to Mexico City, from where he illegally crossed the border to the US in June 2026. On US soil, he was made to purchase laptops, phones, remote access software and wireless networking equipment. He was told that that the company he was monitoring "was providing weapons to fight against Russia in Ukraine."
The Russian officials he was in contact with told him to visit a coffee shop near Palantir's Palo Alto office and take photos of its employees' laptop screens. They also made him switch on his laptop at designated areas near the company's offices, so they could remotely access and collect information from the devices of employees in the vicinity.
His assignment included the surveillance of Palantir employees and their homes, as well. In September, he allegedly followed a female employee in a car for more than 30 miles. D'iu's home was searched on October 8, where authorities found two Russian passports and $18,035 in cash. Authorities had also intercepted packages for him shipped from overseas, containing a fake California ID card and an authentic US passport altered with his photograph.
Palantir, a tech company, is controversial for providing governments, law enforcement and the military products they can then use for mass surveillance. Wired previously reported that ICE used a database built by the company to compile dossiers on people accused of observing and protesting its activities. According to Bloomberg, the US uses Palantir's technology to offer targeting support to Ukraine. In addition, Ukrainian forces in Kyiv use its products for various purposes, including the removal of unexploded Russian mines in the country.
D'iu has been charged with "one count of conspiracy to act as an agent of a foreign government, one count of acting as an agent of a foreign government without notice to the Attorney General, one count of interstate stalking and one count of fraud in connection with identification documents." He is scheduled to appear in federal court on November 24.

articles.title: Đằng sau cảnh người dân Trung Quốc xếp hàng mua vàng miếng nhỏ
articles.text:
Giá vàng lao dốc, các cửa hàng vàng ở nhiều địa phương Trung Quốc, đáng chú ý là tại các thành phố lớn như Bắc Kinh, Thâm Quyến và Thượng Hải chật kín người, vàng miếng 10 gram, 20 gram, 30 gram lần lượt “cháy hàng”.
Nhưng nếu chỉ nhìn vào cảnh xếp hàng để nói rằng người Trung Quốc đang đổ xô “bắt đáy”, có lẽ đã bỏ qua điều quan trọng nhất: đằng sau mỗi giao dịch là một nhu cầu rất cụ thể và đằng sau mỗi sản phẩm được chọn là một thế hệ người tiêu dùng đang thay đổi cách nghĩ về vàng.
Tuần trước, giá vàng giao ngay London giảm 4,56%, chạm 3.832,23 USD/ounce trong phiên 16/11, mức thấp nhất kể từ đầu năm 2025. Đến ngày 18/11, giá tiếp tục thủng mốc 3.800 USD/ounce, có lúc chỉ còn 3.780 USD/ounce, nối dài chuỗi 7 phiên giảm liên tiếp và rơi về vùng giá của tháng 9/2025.
Bà Cù Thụy, chuyên gia của Oriental Jincheng - tổ chức xếp hạng tín nhiệm có uy tín và nổi tiếng hàng đầu tại Trung Quốc, giải thích rằng áp lực lên vàng đến từ 2 kênh. Thứ nhất là lãi suất: lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc Mỹ kỳ hạn 10 năm quay lại trên 5%, làm tăng chi phí cơ hội của việc nắm giữ một tài sản không sinh lãi như vàng.
Thứ hai là tỷ giá: đồng USD mạnh lên khiến vàng - vốn định giá bằng USD trở nên đắt hơn với người nắm giữ các đồng tiền khác. Thị trường hiện định giá khả năng Fed tăng 25 điểm cơ bản vào tháng 12 ở mức hơn 92%.
Tại Trung Quốc, hệ quả là giá vàng trang sức của các thương hiệu lớn giảm mạnh.
Tại khu vực Bách hóa Thái Thị Khẩu ở Bắc Kinh, ngay từ đầu tháng 11, khi giá vàng vừa trượt xuống, cảnh tượng tại quầy vàng miếng đầu tư đã trở nên tấp nập. Nhân viên bán hàng liên tục thông báo: “Vàng miếng dưới 30 gram đều hết”.
Các loại 5 gram, 10 gram, 20 gram cũng cháy hàng. Người mua không rời đi ngay mà vẫn nán lại hỏi “mai có nhập thêm không”, có người tính chuyện “sáng mai đến xếp hàng từ sớm”. Một số khách không muốn chờ đợi thêm đã quyết định mua thẳng 100 gram.
Tại thành phố Thâm Quyến, mức độ còn lớn hơn. Theo dữ liệu được Ngân hàng Thương mại Trung Quốc dẫn lại, cuối tuần có thời điểm chợ vàng Thủy Bối đón khoảng 60.000 lượt khách, trong đó khoảng 70% là người mua vì nhu cầu thực, chủ yếu là cưới hỏi và đeo hàng ngày. Nhiều người kéo theo cả vali đến chọn vàng.
Không phải đầu cơ, mà là “nhu cầu bị dồn nén”
Điểm mấu chốt là ở đây. Đợt mua vàng này không giống một cơn sốt đầu cơ ngắn hạn. Cấu trúc người mua cho thấy một bức tranh rất khác.
Phần lớn là các cặp đôi trẻ, phụ nữ đi theo nhóm và các gia đình. Họ mua dây chuyền, nhẫn, vòng tay nhỏ để tự đeo hoặc chuẩn bị cho đám cưới, đây là những nhu cầu khó trì hoãn thêm.
Bà Cù Thụy gọi đây là sự “giải phóng tập trung” của nhu cầu cưới hỏi, tức các bộ trang sức truyền thống mà nhà trai tặng nhà gái trong lễ cưới, như “tam kim” (3 món vàng: nhẫn, dây chuyền, vòng tay) hoặc “ngũ kim” (5 món vàng, thường thêm hoa tai và lắc chân), cùng nhu cầu đeo vàng hàng ngày vốn bị giá cao kìm lại suốt nhiều tháng.
Nhưng có một thay đổi quan trọng hơn: người mua đang dịch chuyển sang sản phẩm nhỏ, nhẹ. Vàng miếng và trang sức thiết kế mỏng, nhẹ lên ngôi, trông “bắt sáng” và có cảm giác sang trọng, trong khi những chiếc vòng tay lớn, nặng dần mất đi sự ưu ái.
Dữ liệu từ Hội đồng Vàng Thế giới (WGC) cho thấy tỷ lệ nhà bán lẻ ưa chuộng các sản phẩm dưới 10 gram tại quốc gia tỷ dân đã tăng đáng kể so với mức 60% của năm 2025. Không phải vì người ta hết tiền, mà vì họ nhạy cảm hơn với tổng giá trị đơn hàng và phí chế tác khi giá vàng vẫn neo cao.
Đây có lẽ là nghịch lý thú vị nhất mà dữ liệu của WGC hé lộ. Trong quý III/2026, lượng vàng trang sức tiêu thụ tại Trung Quốc giảm 22% so với cùng kỳ, xuống mức thấp nhất cho một quý III kể từ năm 2006.
Nhưng nếu nhìn vào số tiền người dân chi ra, con số lại không hề ít: tổng chi tiêu cho vàng trang sức trong quý đạt 608 tỷ NDT, cao hơn mức trung bình 552 tỷ NDT của một thập kỷ qua.
Nói cách khác, người Trung Quốc mua ít gram hơn, nhưng không nhất thiết chi ít tiền hơn. Họ đang mua những món đồ nhỏ hơn, tinh gọn hơn, phù hợp với nhu cầu “đeo để đẹp” và “tích lũy từng chút một” hơn là phô trương khối lượng.
Đây là một sự thích nghi của thị trường trước một thực tế mới: giá vàng cao đã trở thành “bình thường mới” và người tiêu dùng đang học cách sống chung với nó.
Trong ngắn hạn, phần lớn ý kiến đều thận trọng. Bà Cù Thụy nhận định giá vàng sẽ dao động mạnh, phụ thuộc vào dữ liệu và tích lũy trong biên độ. Trước khi kỳ vọng tăng lãi suất hạ nhiệt rõ ràng, đà phục hồi của vàng sẽ bị giới hạn.
Chuyên gia Đinh Trăn Vũ từ Công ty Tư vấn Đầu tư Cự Phong Thiểm Tây cũng cho rằng ngắn hạn giá sẽ đi ngang trong biên độ, chịu ảnh hưởng từ kỳ vọng lãi suất và hoạt động mua ròng của ngân hàng trung ương.
Nhưng về dài hạn, logic nền tảng vẫn chưa bị đảo ngược. WGC dự báo tiêu dùng vàng trang sức tại Trung Quốc trong quý IV sẽ tiếp tục phục hồi theo mùa, với 2 nhóm sản phẩm tiếp tục được ưa chuộng: vàng cứng (vàng nguyên chất được xử lý để cứng hơn, ít biến dạng, phù hợp với thiết kế tinh xảo và đeo hàng ngày) và vàng cổ truyền (chế tác thủ công theo kỹ thuật cổ, bề mặt sần mờ đặc trưng, được ưa chuộng vì nét truyền thống).
Nhu cầu đầu tư vàng cũng được kỳ vọng duy trì ở mức mạnh, đặc biệt khi bất ổn địa chính trị toàn cầu còn hiện hữu.
Theo Securities Daily, 21st Century Business Herald, WGC, China Business Herald, CNR

articles.title: Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are cheaper than ever for Black Friday
articles.text:
Back in my day, the only “Doorbuster” sales were at physical retail stores. But now, you can get ultra-low prices before Black Friday whether you want to shop in-store or online. One that stands out is the previous-generation Sony WH-1000XM5 noise-canceling headphones, which are marked down to their lowest price ever, just $169.99 at Best Buy. While their MSRP is $399.99, they’ve been spotted as low as $198 in the last few months.
Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are cheaper than ever for Black Friday
Last-generation noise-cancelling headphones are still a great option for traveling or staying focused.
The WH-1000XM5 launched in 2022, and despite having been succeeded by the WH-1000XM6, they’re still an excellent set of headphones. Their active noise cancellation effect is one of the best out there — competitive with the latest models from Bose and Apple — and the sound profile is tighter and more balanced than the older Sony headphones. There are some minor downsides, like a bulky case and all-plastic design, but those seem easier to overlook at this lower price point.
The newer Sony WH-1000XM6 improve the sound and noise cancellation, with quality of life upgrades not present in the XM5, like a folding design and more comfortable headband. However, they’re significantly more expensive, currently discounted to $348 during Black Friday (Amazon, Best Buy), down from their MSRP of $450.
To make shopping a little more confusing, the newer WH-1000XM4C sit between the XM5 and XM6 in terms of price, and are a slightly updated version of the older XM4 model with its foldable design. Our reviewer John Higgins thinks the XM4C’s noise cancellation lags behind, so I’d opt for the XM5 over them, especially at the sale price.

articles.title: Google's Gemini can now take over tasks on your Mac
articles.text:
Google is rolling out computer use in its Gemini app for Mac, letting the assistant carry out multi-step tasks across local files, desktop apps and websites in a separate background window. It is for paying AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers, and Google warns it can make mistakes, including deleting or sharing files.
Google’s Gemini assistant can now take over tasks on a Mac, clicking through apps, typing and filling in forms for you. Google announced on Thursday that computer use is rolling out in the Gemini app for Mac.
You describe a task, and Gemini works through it across local files, desktop apps and websites. It runs in a separate background window with a live preview in the chat, so your screen and cursor stay free. You choose which apps it can use, can pause it, and must approve key actions.
Google’s examples include pulling weights and addresses from PDFs into a shipping quote form, and turning dashboard data into a Google Slides deck. It can also batch-edit photos or prepare resale listings from pictures in a folder.
The feature is for paying subscribers to Google’s AI Plus, Pro and Ultra plans, and needs a Mac with Apple Silicon. As with its Gemini Spark agent, it is not available in Europe or the UK. Google first built computer use into Gemini 3.5 Flash for developers in June.
Google warns that Gemini can make mistakes, including permanently deleting files or sharing them with others. It is designed to ask permission first, and it can only see folders you connect. Backups of changed files are deleted after 24 hours or when you start a new task.
Google is also building Gemini into the operating system of its Googlebook laptops, as rivals race to put agents on the desktop. OpenAI’s ChatGPT can log your keystrokes on a Mac to build its memory. Agents built on the OpenClaw framework have helped drive Mac mini demand.

articles.title: Nimble enters the item-tracking market with eco-friendly luggage tags and keychains | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As Google steps up its competition with Apple in the item-tracking market, smaller brands are also looking to carve out a piece of the category. The latest entrant is Nimble, the sustainable accessories brand best known for its charging products.
Founded in 2018 by former Mophie executives, the California-based company announced Thursday that it’s expanding into the category with “Trace,” a seven-product collection of item trackers designed to blend tracking technology into everyday accessories.
Nimble’s new collection arrives as competition in the Bluetooth tracking market continues to heat up. Apple’s AirTag helped popularize the category, while Google recently introduced its first-party tracker, the $29 Pixel Tag, powered by its Find Hub network. Meanwhile, established third-party players, such as Chipolo and Pebblebee, continue to expand their lineups.
Nimble is taking a slightly different approach. Rather than introducing another stand-alone tracker to attach to a set of keys or slip into a bag, the company has integrated tracking technology directly into practical accessories, including wallets, keychains, luggage tags, and passport covers.
The lineup includes seven products, ranging from the $14.95 Trace Tag, which features a replaceable coin-cell battery, to the $49.95 Trace Folio, a passport cover with built-in rechargeable tracking. Other options include the Trace Keyfob ($19.95), Trace Slim Wallet Card ($29.95), Trace Keychain ($29.95), Trace Luggage Tag ($39.95), and Trace Wallet ($39.95).
The entire collection is compatible with both Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub networks.
Ross Howe, co-founder and CEO of Nimble, told us that the company’s approach is designed to differentiate its products from traditional trackers.
“Most locators are built as utility gadgets, not as things you want to own. Few were asking why the locator couldn’t just be the nice object itself. So, for example, we made a wallet findable instead of making a tracker that fits a wallet. We also thought more options should be rechargeable.”
The Trace Luggage Tag and Trace Folio are arguably the most interesting products in the collection. Dedicated luggage tags and passport covers with built-in tracking remain relatively uncommon, giving Nimble an opportunity to stand out in a market. There are only a few alternatives, including Spotminder’s $59 passport cover with Apple Find My support, which is $10 more than Nimble’s option. Knog Scout offers a luggage tag, although I find its design a little too bulky.
Rechargeability is another appealing aspect of Nimble’s new collection. Several models support USB-C or wireless charging, offering an alternative to the disposable batteries found in many traditional trackers. Howe says battery life lasts for “months,” with the Trace Keyfob, for example, rated for approximately six months on a charge.
Sustainability is another major part of Nimble’s pitch. Staying true to its roots, the company has incorporated eco-friendly materials throughout the collection, including recycled plastics and plant-based, vegan aloe leather. The products have also undergone third-party testing for chemicals of concern.
“We’ve spent the last two years going through the chemistry of our products line by line to remove or limit as many harmful ingredients as possible. Trace is the first collection designed specifically to meet these higher standards. We’re not 100% yet, but the independent labs checking our work will help us get there,” Howe said.
The collection is available now through its website and Amazon. All seven products come in five color options: Black, Stone, Tangerine, Plum, and Teal.

articles.title: Elon Musk accuses Ukraine of being 'untruthful' about Starshield disruptions - Engadget
articles.text:
Elon Musk accuses Ukraine of being 'untruthful' about Starshield disruptions
He said that Ukraine is trying to use SpaceX’s consumer Starlink service for military purposes.
Elon Musk has accused Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy of being "untruthful" about Starshield disruptions hampering the nation's ability to defend and fight back against Russia. The SpaceX CEO told The New York Times' DealBook Summit that Ukraine is actually trying to use the company's consumer Starlink service, not Starshield, for military purposes.
"From the beginning, I've said that Starlink is a civilian system," Musk told interviewer Andrew Ross Sorkin. "It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to use Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government. But do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions."
Musk's comments come amid a lengthy disruption to Starshield in Ukraine. Last month, Zelenskyy posted on X that speed limits on Starshield were imposed along the war's entire front line and in Russian territory, saying any terminal moving faster than 161 km/h (100 mph) would lose its connection to the satellite network. "Unfortunately, this is helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine," Zelenskyy said at the time. "We are trying to establish all the circumstances with the American side."
Sorkin reminded Musk that Zelenskyy referred to the system being slowed down as Starshield and not Starlink. "That's false... [Zelenskyy is] not always truthful," Musk replied. "What he is actually saying is he wants to use Starlink for offensive military operations."
The last time Starshield was slowed on October 14, SpaceX and The White House blamed each other for throttling speeds, but nothing was ever confirmed. Citing US officials, Reuters had reported that the order came from inside the White House. Later on, though, The Wall Street Journal's sources said that Musk himself ordered the slowdown.
Later in October, Ukraine pushed back against allegations that it had misused Starlink for offensive attacks. An official said that pre-existing restrictions on the systems would have made it "physically impossible" for Ukraine to use Starlink to strike in Russian territory as Musk described.

articles.title: Model ML raises $250m at a $1.5bn valuation for AI agents in banks
articles.text:
Model ML, a London startup that builds AI agents for bankers, consultants and investors, has raised $250m at a $1.5bn valuation. General Atlantic and QED Investors co-led the Series B round, the company said on Tuesday.
Evolution Equity Partners, Airtree, Forestay Capital, Y Combinator, FT Partners, Latitude, Inception Fund and 13Books Capital also took part. The round takes Model ML’s total funding to $350m. FT Partners led its $75m Series A in November 2025, and HSBC Asset Management invested in August.
In the third quarter, Model ML’s annual recurring revenue grew 12 times year on year and its daily active users rose 26 times, the company said. It will use the money to grow its research and engineering teams in London and New York.
An agent for every banker
Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander founded Model ML in 2023, Bloomberg reported. They previously co-founded Fat Llama, a rental marketplace that Sweden’s Hygglo bought for $41.5m in 2022, TechCrunch reported.
Each user gets an agent that runs on the firm’s own systems and data. When news breaks on a company a banker covers, the agent judges whether it matters and prepares the analysis in the firm’s formats. It works in tools such as Excel and PowerPoint to build pitch decks and due diligence reports.
“AI should do more than give you another answer or notification. It should understand your work and get things done,” said Chaz Englander, Model ML’s co-founder and CEO.
Model ML sends each task to the AI model that suits it best. A growing share runs on its own fine-tuned open-source models. On the work they handle, these cost 2% as much as frontier models and are in most cases five times faster, the company said. It added that customer data is never used to train AI models.
Job cuts and the CEO’s pitch
Banks have tied job cuts to AI. Barclays said in October it would cut 5,000 jobs, and Standard Chartered plans to cut 7,800 jobs in back-office roles by 2030. Englander played down the idea that Model ML is mainly a way to cut costs.
“The average age of a Model ML user is 33 years old, not 23 years old,” Englander told Bloomberg. “These tools are no longer productivity and efficiency tools. They’re revenue generative.”
Revenue is split fairly evenly across banks, consulting firms and asset managers, he said. Model ML’s rivals include New York’s Rogo, which raised $160m at a $2bn valuation in April. OpenAI and Anthropic also sell AI tools to financial professionals.

articles.title: You can now buy a Steam Machine without getting on a waitlist
articles.text:
Valve announced some updates about Steam Machine availability today, including good news if you want to buy one right now and potential bad news about future supply due to RAMaggedon.
You can now buy a Steam Machine without getting on a waitlist
Valve’s 512GB Steam Machine is available to buy now, but the 2TB model is out of stock.
The good news: You can now purchase a 512GB Steam Machine without getting on a waitlist. Initially, interested buyers had to get on Valve’s waitlist if they wanted to purchase one, but the console-like PC is now available in an “add-to-cart” status, according to the company. As I write this, the 512GB versions with and without a bundled controller are showing estimated delivery dates of three to five business days on Valve’s website. If Valve sells through its current inventory, the company says it will indicate that the product is out of stock instead of making another waitlist.
The bad news: If you’re on the waitlist for a 2TB model, you might not get a chance to buy one at all, as Valve says there are more people on the waitlist than there are units available. The company is closing the waitlists for its 2TB models.
Valve says that while it’s still building more Steam machines, “memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels” and that it doesn’t know the number it can make or “at what price we’ll be able to offer them.” The 2TB Steam Machine is “especially constrained.” The company anticipates “having more information” to share about additional supply in January.
After delaying the Steam Machine’s expected early 2026 launch due to the memory and storage crisis, Valve launched the product in June with a price starting at $1,049 for the 512GB model without a bundled controller. A 2TB model without a controller costs $1,349.

articles.title: Bỏ đàn bò, đầu tư 2 tỷ đồng làm homestay dưới chân núi Ba Vì
articles.text:
Từ đàn bò sữa đến quyết định đầu tư tiền tỷ
Trước năm 2014, thôn Xoan, nay thuộc thôn Vân Sơn, xã Yên Bài, còn nhiều khó khăn. Sinh kế của người dân chủ yếu dựa vào trồng trọt, chăn nuôi. Không ít gia đình phải lên rừng tìm măng, hái cây lá đem về ăn hoặc bán kiếm thêm thu nhập. Những mô hình như trồng ớt, trồng vầu, nuôi giun, nuôi nhím lần lượt được thử nghiệm nhưng không phải hướng đi nào cũng mang lại hiệu quả.
Gia đình chị Đinh Thị Hường, một người Mường gốc ở địa phương, cũng từng trải qua nhiều lần chuyển đổi sinh kế. Năm 2014, gia đình vay 50 triệu đồng từ Ngân hàng Chính sách xã hội để đầu tư nuôi khoảng 20 con lợn nái và 30 con lợn thịt. Thời gian đầu, chăn nuôi có lãi. Tuy nhiên, giá lợn hơi từ mức 45.000-50.000 đồng/kg có lúc giảm còn 14.000-15.000 đồng/kg, khiến gia đình thua lỗ.
Không bỏ cuộc, chị Hường tiếp tục vay vốn, thế chấp quyền sử dụng đất để vay vốn đầu tư nuôi bò. Từ 2 con bò cái nuôi năm 2016, đến năm 2022, đàn bò phát triển lên 14 con. Nhờ bò sữa, mỗi tháng gia đình thu về hơn 10 triệu đồng sau khi trừ chi phí.
Dù kinh tế ổn định hơn, công việc chăn nuôi vẫn rất vất vả, từ chuẩn bị thức ăn, vệ sinh chuồng trại đến theo dõi sức khỏe. Cuộc sống của gia đình chị gần như gắn chặt với chuồng trại, không có thời gian nghỉ ngơi.
Trong khi đó, vùng đất dưới chân núi Ba Vì ngày càng thu hút người từ Hà Nội tìm về mua đất, đầu tư xây dựng homestay, villa và các khu nghỉ dưỡng. Năm 2022, chị Hường có thời gian làm nhân viên kinh doanh tại một cơ sở lưu trú. Qua công việc này, chị nhận thấy mô hình kinh doanh du lịch có tiềm năng mang lại nguồn thu tốt hơn so với chăn nuôi.
Do đó, chị quyết định chuyển hướng kinh doanh trên chính mảnh đất của gia đình. Sau nhiều năm gắn bó với chăn nuôi, chị bán toàn bộ đàn bò, thu về hơn 300 triệu đồng. Gia đình vay thêm 1,5 tỷ đồng từ ngân hàng, kết hợp vốn tự có, đầu tư tổng cộng khoảng 2 tỷ đồng xây dựng Phúc Hưng Homestay.
Cơ sở lưu trú nằm trên khu đất rộng hơn 2.000m2, trong đó khoảng 400m2 là không gian sinh sống của gia đình, diện tích còn lại dành cho kinh doanh. Công trình nhà hai tầng có 9 phòng nghỉ, nằm trên trục đường chính dẫn vào khu du lịch Thiên Sơn - Suối Ngà.
Chia sẻ với PV VietNamNet, chị Hường cho hay giai đoạn 2023-2025, hoạt động homestay mang lại nguồn thu tốt hơn nhiều so với chăn nuôi bò sữa trước đây. Công việc cũng nhẹ nhàng hơn, giúp gia đình chủ động thời gian và có thêm cơ hội phát triển các hoạt động kinh doanh khác.
Ngoài ra, gia đình chị còn tận dụng diện tích từng trồng cỏ để trồng đào bán dịp Tết và cây công trình. Sản phẩm có đầu ra nhờ nhu cầu trang trí, hoàn thiện cảnh quan của các homestay, khu nghỉ dưỡng.
Du lịch đánh thức tiềm năng vùng đất dưới chân núi
Câu chuyện của gia đình chị Hường phản ánh sự thay đổi trong cách người dân Vân Sơn nhìn nhận cơ hội phát triển kinh tế. Thực tế, du lịch tại khu vực này không phải mới xuất hiện. Những điều kiện để hình thành vùng nghỉ dưỡng đã được tích lũy từ nhiều thập kỷ trước.
Thôn Xoan, Nghe và Rùa trước đây, nay được gộp thành thôn Vân Sơn, nằm gần nhiều điểm du lịch nổi tiếng ở sườn phía đông núi Ba Vì. Cổng Vườn quốc gia Ba Vì cách khu dân cư khoảng 2,5km; khu du lịch Thiên Sơn - Suối Ngà cách nhà chị Hường khoảng 400m. Khoang Xanh - Suối Tiên được đầu tư khai thác từ những năm 1990, trong khi khu du lịch Long Việt hình thành sau năm 2010.
Các địa điểm này thu hút đông đảo du khách. Người dân có thêm cơ hội bán hàng ăn, nông sản, sản vật và đồ lưu niệm, hoặc làm việc tại các khu du lịch. Những sản phẩm quen thuộc như củ sắn, bắp ngô, đậu lạc, nếp nương cũng trở thành hàng hóa phục vụ khách tham quan.
Tuy nhiên, trong thời gian dài, người dân chủ yếu tham gia hoạt động du lịch với vai trò phụ trợ, cung cấp lao động hoặc dịch vụ nhỏ lẻ. Chỉ khi xu hướng nghỉ dưỡng cuối tuần, lưu trú gần thiên nhiên phát triển, nhiều hộ mới mạnh dạn đầu tư homestay, villa để trực tiếp kinh doanh.
Ông Nguyễn Ngọc Linh, Trưởng thôn Vân Sơn, cho biết du lịch địa phương phát triển mạnh trong những năm gần đây nhờ lợi thế nằm dưới chân núi Ba Vì, cùng hệ thống giao thông, cầu cống và điện lưới ngày càng được hoàn thiện.
Không chỉ tham gia cung cấp lao động, nông sản và các dịch vụ nhỏ lẻ, nhiều hộ dân đã trực tiếp đầu tư cơ sở lưu trú, kinh doanh ăn uống và các dịch vụ phục vụ khách nghỉ dưỡng.
Vân Sơn hiện có 564 hộ, trong đó khoảng 50% là người dân tộc Mường. Toàn thôn có 27 cơ sở du lịch nghỉ dưỡng. Một số cơ sở do người địa phương đầu tư gồm Phúc Hưng của gia đình chị Hường, Gia Khánh của bà Dương Liễu, T-House của ông Nguyễn Văn Thành, Dương Gia Homestay của ông Nguyễn Văn Tụ và cơ sở của gia đình bà Lan.
Sự xuất hiện của các cơ sở lưu trú cho thấy một bộ phận người dân, trong đó có nhiều hộ người Mường, đang chuyển từ tham gia các dịch vụ phụ trợ sang trực tiếp kinh doanh du lịch.
Từ đàn bò sữa đến homestay, từ những thửa đất trồng cỏ đến vườn đào, cây cảnh, câu chuyện của gia đình chị Hường là một ví dụ về cách người dân tận dụng lợi thế cảnh quan và nhu cầu nghỉ dưỡng để tìm hướng sinh kế mới. Hoạt động du lịch không chỉ tạo nguồn thu cho các chủ cơ sở lưu trú mà còn mở thêm cơ hội việc làm, tiêu thụ nông sản và phát triển các dịch vụ đi kèm tại địa phương.

articles.title: Superhuman pushes its Go assistant everywhere | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Productivity apps are simultaneously trying to feed more context to their AI tools while also making those AI assistants available in every nook and corner of their products. Superhuman (formerly Grammarly) is going in the same direction with the rollout of features, including a personalized Go assistant, making agents available in Docs, and third-party agent integrations.
While some of the company’s AI features have faced criticism, Superhuman started pushing its Go assistant after its rebranding last year. With the new rollout, it is making Go learn context across different apps and give better personalized suggestions for prompts. Superhuman is revamping its onboarding flow to let users connect their preferred tools and load context about their work upfront.
The assistant works inline with the cursor — just like Grammarly — and also manages other agents. Superhuman is also making the agent proactive, which means it looks for your schedule, keeps an eye on your email, and even drafts responses. The updated Go agent also learns users’ writing styles and responds accordingly in email and Docs.
The productivity company is adding 20 new connected agents, including DeepL, Legora, Amplitude, Databricks, and Blackboard, through its Go SDK.
The company is also thinking about adding AI to different products, including Docs and Superhuman Mail. In Docs, all Go agents work natively, and you can set them off to work on different tasks in the background. Users can also set routines to trigger workflows based on events.
Until now, Mail has used AI as its central tool, which is being replaced by Go. Users can also do enterprise search by using data from the company knowledge base and connected tools. Go also uses this context to form drafts and organize the inbox across Google and Outlook accounts.
Superhuman acquired notetaker Fathom in September to add more context to its suite. The company is now rolling out live collaborative notetaking, which would be shared across the team. Plus, Go can now make decisions post-meeting, like forming an initial draft of a proposal.
The company’s CEO, Shishir Mehrotra, said that Go has had good momentum with over 1 million active users. There are a host of agents now that are vying for users’ attention on both the personal and professional front. Mehrotra thinks that while Go is more work-focused, it can help with personal emails and schedules.
“One of the reasons why these assistants have been popular is that they treat you as a whole person and recognize that we need to cover both extremes. Go is definitely more work-focused than some of the tools coming out of the pure consumer ecosystem. It doesn’t mean we draw the boundary at helping you with your personal tasks or helping you with your calendar or all of your email,” he told TechCrunch over a call.
While Go might not directly compete with the likes of Instinct, Muse, and Fo, Superhuman wants users to choose its assistant over something like OpenAI’s Dots or Claude Duet.

articles.title: Some creators are skeptical of Instagram’s new affiliate program
articles.text:
For years, influencers have come up with workarounds on social media to figure out how to share affiliate links with followers. A new integration between Instagram and Amazon was announced earlier this month as a way to make it easier for influencers to make money from affiliate links — but some content creators are suspicious about who really benefits.
Some creators are skeptical of Instagram’s new affiliate program
Influencers are now able to link their Amazon and Instagram accounts to promote products. Some are concerned about what they’re opting in to.
The new integration allows creators to connect their Instagram and Amazon accounts and automatically tag products with their affiliate links, from which they earn a commission when followers make purchases. Influencers will be able to embed up to 30 product links in a Reel or 20 in a feed post, but a permissions setting has led to concerns about what creators are actually agreeing to.
In connecting an Amazon account, creators must agree to allow the retailer and its brand sellers to create ads from “any public content” that includes a related affiliate link. Influencers must also agree to acknowledge that brands can edit their content and use their “testimonial, caption or media” for ads.
The wide-ranging permissions are giving creators pause. Some have urged peers not to connect their accounts without reviewing the permissions and understanding how the feature would affect earnings. People making money on social media spend years tweaking their content and strategy to maximize reach, engagement, and, by extension, their bottom line. For some, it appeared that they would be giving Amazon and its sellers the ability to use their content under unclear terms. On Instagram head Adam Mosseri’s post announcing the feature, influencers complained about the lack of clarity, questioned whether using the feature would decrease their reach (which some creators say happens when they link to outside products), and demanded answers to whether their commission rate would stay the same when Amazon or brands use their content for ads.
Linking products through the new integration won’t reduce reach, Jimmy O’Keefe, Instagram’s director of product marketing, said in an email to The Verge. O’Keefe also noted that creators will continue to earn commission through affiliate links when Amazon boosts their posts, and that they can stop the boosting in settings or disconnect the integration entirely. There’s also a separate, manual way to add products without linking accounts, if a creator wants to opt out of having their content made into ads.
Amazon has an enormous influencer program that reaches across social media platforms. It is so lucrative that some content creators are able to make a living almost exclusively by hawking products for sale on Amazon, building empires on the shopping habits of their followers. When it comes to putting those links in front of followers, though, social platforms have historically been a roadblock, hence the cottage industry of link-in-bio tools meant to circumvent limits. Slowly but surely, though, platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube — perhaps chasing the success of TikTok Shop — have added more and more shopping features. The result is that shopping and social media begin to feel more and more like the same thing.

articles.title: Anthropic shares jump 34% at open in record Nasdaq debut
articles.text:
Anthropic’s shares opened at $111.50 on Nasdaq on Thursday, 34% above the $83 IPO price, valuing it at more than $2T, per Business Insider. The company raised $107.3B with its IPO and a private placement, the largest listing on record.
Anthropic’s shares opened at $111.50 on Nasdaq on Thursday, 34% above their $83 IPO price, Business Insider reported. The jump, bigger than the 27% grey markets had pointed to, valued the Claude maker at more than $2T. The stock trades under the ticker ANT.
Dario and Daniela Amodei rang the opening bell with staff earlier in the day. By midday in New York, the shares had eased to about $107, still up nearly 29%, according to Bloomberg data.
The open beat SpaceX’s debut in June. SpaceX, which priced its IPO at $135 a share, opened 11% higher and closed its first day up 19%.
Anthropic raised about $81B by selling shares at $83 on Wednesday, above its $70 to $78 range. It is also raising $26B from a private placement at the same price, with Alphabet, Microsoft and Nvidia among the buyers. Together, that makes $107.3B, the biggest IPO on record.
The debut lifted the wider market, with the Nasdaq Composite up more than 1% after the open. As the first big pure-play AI stock, Anthropic is likely to be watched as a test of investors’ appetite for AI.
Not everyone is convinced. In October, research firm New Constructs said Anthropic might be worth as little as $144B. On Wednesday, a group of scientists signed a statement calling it “not a safe AI company”.

articles.title: Sonos is taking up to 30 percent off speakers and soundbars right now
articles.text:
Sonos speakers and soundbars aren’t exactly cheap, but thankfully the company’s Black Friday sale has already begun, making everything a little easier to afford through November 30th. Most notably, you can pick up the Arc Ultra soundbar for a new low of $849 ($250 off) from Sonos, Amazon, and Best Buy, or the newfangled Sonos Play for $239 ($60 off) from the same retailers (Sonos, Amazon, Best Buy).
Sonos is taking up to 30 percent off speakers and soundbars right now
Whether you want a portable speaker or a new home theater setup, Sonos is offering great deals through November 30th.
If you’re looking to give your home theater setup a big upgrade, the Arc Ultra is an excellent soundbar. It supports Dolby Atmos and delivers more immersive sound than the original Arc, while adding Bluetooth connectivity. Dialogue also sounds noticeably clearer, and the new Quick Tune feature automatically adjusts the soundbar’s audio to suit your room using built-in microphones, so you no longer need an iPhone to fine-tune the sound for your environment. For more powerful bass, you can also pair it with a compatible Sonos subwoofer, like the Sub 4, which is also available from Sonos as part of a discounted bundle for $1,499 ($499 off).
If you’re looking for a more affordable soundbar, the second-gen Sonos Beam has also hit a new low price at Amazon, Best Buy, and Sonos’ online storefront, where you can buy it for $339 ($160 off). The sound isn’t quite as immersive as that of the Arc Ultra, but the latest Beam can still fill a room with rich, clear audio. It also supports Dolby Atmos; however, unlike the newer Beam Ultra, it lacks side- and upward-firing speakers and instead relies on software to replicate surround sound effects. It also supports HDMI eARC, providing high-quality audio from a compatible TV.
If you’re shopping for a smart speaker instead of a soundbar, the Era 100 SL is available for an all-time low of $149 ($40 off) from Sonos, Amazon, and Best Buy (the standard Era 100 is also down to $179 at Amazon and Best Buy). The feature-packed speakers are nearly identical, but the SL model lacks a built-in mic, and thus voice controls. Both offer excellent stereo sound and rich bass, with dual tweeters and a large woofer that delivers clear, detailed audio despite its small size. They also support Bluetooth and Apple’s AirPlay 2, and you can connect a wired audio source like a turntable using an optional USB-C adapter. For a more immersive experience, you can even pair two for stereo sound or use them as rear surrounds with a compatible Sonos soundbar.
If you want a speaker you can take on the go, the newer Sonos Play is available from Sonos, Amazon, and Best Buy for $239 ($60 off), which is the first notable discount we’ve seen. The portable speaker delivers clear, detailed sound that can fill both larger rooms and outdoor spaces. It also offers up to 24 hours of battery life and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance, making it a great companion for long days at the beach or other outdoor adventures. Plus, its removable carrying loop makes it easy to bring along, and you can even use it to top off your phone. Like other Sonos speakers, it supports both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and you can also group it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when you’re outdoors and away from Wi-Fi.
Last but not least, you can also buy the Sonos Ace for $229 ($120 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and directly from Sonos, which marks a new low price. The newer Ace Ultra offer better sound and improved noise cancellation, but the Ace is still a solid option, especially if you already own a Sonos soundbar. The gorgeous headphones deliver powerful, detailed sound, solid noise cancellation, and an exceptionally natural-sounding transparency mode, along with up to 30 hours of continuous playback on a single charge. Unlike the newer Ultra, though, they can’t transfer music from your other Sonos speakers to your headphones. However, their TV Audio Swap feature still lets you transfer audio from a compatible Sonos soundbar to your headphones, so you can watch movies or listen to music playing on your TV without disturbing anyone else.

articles.title: Anthropic IPO 'exactly what the markets need', but analysts warn of volatility
articles.text:
Anthropic's blockbuster IPO on Thursday gave markets a much-needed boost after weeks of weakness, though analysts warned that the stock could remain volatile in the coming weeks.
Share of the Claude maker opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 per share, 17% above the IPO price. The offering raised $81.3 billion through the sale of 980 million shares — surpassing SpaceX's June listing to become the largest IPO on record.
For investors, it's going to become a blue-chip stock like Google.Ross GerberCEO, Gerber Kawasaki
Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott described investors as "foaming at the mouth" for the offering, with allocations "impossibly low," underscoring the strength of demand.
"Anthropic's IPO is exactly what the markets need to revive overall sentiment," said Rebecca Walser, chief investment officer at Walser Wealth Management, adding that markets have been "depressed with all of the negativity in the AI complex over the past several weeks."
While the initial pop was not surprising for such a highly anticipated listing, investors should avoid "chasing the IPO," Walser said.
She expects the stock to come under pressure in the coming weeks as former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang testifies before the U.S. Senate, potentially reviving concerns around the AI sector once again.
"The shares remain highly volatile," said Morningstar senior equity analyst Malik Ahmed Khan.
Walser said that any weakness around the testimony could offer an entry point for investors interested in Anthropic, adding that she remains bullish on the OpenAI rival over the long term.
"For investors, it's going to become a blue-chip stock like Google," Ross Gerber, president and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management told CNBC.
He added that U.S. technology valuations are at ridiculously low levels relative to the "crazy amazing innovation" coming out of California.
Morningstar's Khan struck a more cautious tone, warning investors against getting swept up in the enthusiasm around Anthropic, advising them instead to step back and "carefully" assess the company as a long-term business.
That will depend on Anthropic's ability to scale enterprise adoption, continue improving its models and turn those capabilities into economically useful products and services in the AI ecosystem, he said.
"We remain confident that the firm will be able to execute on all three fronts," Khan added, setting a $92 fair value estimate for the stock.
Walser stated that Anthropic is "extremely important for the overall AI story" as the first non-Chinese large language model developer to go public.
Its listing gives public-market investors their first direct test of how a major standalone AI model developer will be valued and perform outside the chip sector. Meanwhile, rival OpenAI could follow with an IPO sometime in 2027.
"This IPO is the show me moment for the AI story," Walser said, as much of the stock market's AI narrative has so far centered on chipmakers.

articles.title: SoftBank plunges over 16% as AI sell-off hits Asian tech stocks following Anthropic debut
articles.text:
Shares of Japan's SoftBank Group plunged 16.16% on Friday, leading a broader sell-off in Asian technology stocks following the highly anticipated market debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic.
SoftBank is one of the biggest backers of OpenAI, Anthropic's rival, having invested a total of $64.6 billion in the ChatGPT maker.
The sharp decline underscores growing investor concerns over SoftBank's aggressive bets on artificial intelligence, particularly its exposure to OpenAI, as markets question whether massive investments in AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.
SoftBank's heavy exposure to OpenAI has made its shares particularly sensitive to shifts in sentiment toward the AI sector. The stock lost 30% in October and is down 31% so far this month.
If Friday's losses hold, it would be SoftBank's worst day in more than two years.
Japanese semiconductor stocks also tumbled, with Tokyo Electron falling 7.19%, Lasertec declining 6.75% and Renesas Electronics dropping 6.71%.
The sell-off extended to South Korea, where Nvidia suppliers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics dropped 6% and 4.7%, respectively. South Korea's benchmark Kospi also declined 3.66%.
The declines in Asia come after the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% overnight following Anthropic's highly anticipated Wall Street debut.

articles.title: Lumentum CEO defends Marvell deal after stock plunge: 'We've got work to do' with shareholders
articles.text:
Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston defended the company's planned merger with chipmaker Marvell Technology on Thursday, acknowledging that the deal has received a disappointing reception.
"Their numbers are phenomenal. Our numbers are phenomenal, and we feel the combination is even more powerful," Hurlston told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." Nevertheless, Hurlston said, "Shareholders are not happy ... It's been a tough couple of weeks."
Shares of Marvell and Lumentum have tumbled 45% and 42%, respectively, since the close on Oct. 28. That night, Bloomberg News reported Marvell was nearing a megadeal to buy Lumentum, sending shockwaves through the market and beginning the wild ride that both stocks have been on. The tie-up was officially announced on the morning of Nov. 2 with the deal expected to close in the first half of 2028. At the time, the all-stock deal implied an enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum.
Beginning on Oct. 29, Marvell shares experienced three straight days of double-digit percentage declines. In total, they've advanced in just three sessions since the Oct. 28 close. For its part, Lumentum rose modestly on Oct. 29 following the initial M&A rumor. Then the selling pressure arrived, as investors questioned the merits of the deal. The stock has been green in five sessions since the Bloomberg report.
The merger would combine Marvell's semiconductor and networking technology with Lumentum's optical components as AI data centers increasingly shift from copper wiring to fiber-optic connections to handle faster data transmission. Hurlston said that transition, rather than simply the construction of more data centers, will be a major growth driver for the planned combined entity.
"We've got work to do with our shareholders," Hurlston said, though he sees catalysts on the horizon that could help change their minds. He pointed to Marvell's earnings report scheduled for Dec. 1 and the upcoming release of a securities filing, known as an S-4, required as part of the merger process.
"As people see [Marvell CEO Matt Murphy's] earnings he's going to announce in early December, we've got the S-4 coming out that's going to describe how both businesses are performing, we've got our earnings … I think those things together will give the shareholders confidence that, look, there's nothing wrong here. I mean, these businesses are great, and they're even better together," said Hurlston, who has led Lumentum since February 2025.
To be sure, the dramatic decline in both Marvell and Lumentum shares isn't entirely due to the investor displeasure with the planned transaction. In recent weeks, the market has soured on the AI trade more broadly, amid questions about the sustainability of the AI buildout due to higher borrowing costs and political backlash on data center construction, which was exemplified by the midterm election results. Though Hurlston acknowledged these other forces affecting the stocks and leading to compressed valuation multiples, he emphasized the work that he needs to do to win shareholder support.
Despite concerns about the broader AI buildout, Hurlston said Lumentum has seen no slowdown in demand. The company reported better-than-expected quarterly results on the day the merger was announced, with revenue more than doubling from a year earlier.
"I think we're going to get that multiple back once we can show our numbers and show how strong the two businesses are doing," he said.

articles.title: Cramer: My favorite chartist sees two major signs of a rally brewing in Alphabet stock
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Thursday that Alphabet looks ready to rebound, based on analysis from his longtime favorite chartist Larry Williams.
"I'm tempted to start to look for opportunities as this brutal market brings down so many stocks, especially in tech," the "Mad Money" host said. "Williams thinks he's found a good one in Alphabet, where the fundamentals and the technicals seem to be coming along very well."
While always cautious about speculative and unprofitable companies, Cramer said that recent market declines have made stocks with strong earnings and real growth increasingly attractive. Technology stocks, particularly those tied to artificial intelligence, have come under pressure over the past couple of months after leading Wall Street's rally earlier this year. Investors have grown increasingly concerned about whether the massive spending on AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns. Elevated valuations, higher interest rates, and fears of a slowdown in data center construction have also added to the pressure.
On the fundamental side, Alphabet stands out to Williams on valuation.
The Google parent's stock is trading at roughly 15 times full-year 2026 earnings estimates, well below its 20 to 30 times multiple over the past five years. According to Williams' chart, the current price-to-earnings valuation level (blue P/E line and left vertical axis) is almost where shares bottomed in the spring of 2025, before the stock price (red GOOGL line) more than doubled in just over a year, including its recent pullback. This is significant because when the stock got this cheap early last year, investors started pouring into the name.
Williams also sees encouraging signs in the technicals.
To explain his analysis, Cramer examined charts tracking two of the technician's proprietary indicators: professional accumulation, which measures buying activity among large investors (red line), and a valuation model (blue line) that identifies when a stock may be undervalued. Historically, when professional accumulation has reached elevated levels (top two circles) while Williams' valuation model signals that Alphabet is undervalued (bottom two circles), the combination has coincided with bottoms in the stock price (black line above), followed by significant rallies.
That pattern emerged earlier this year, preceding a sharp rally in Alphabet shares. And now, Williams sees a similar setup developing, with his valuation model showing the stock as undervalued while professional investors have been aggressively accumulating shares over the past four weeks. "This pattern, as Williams sees it, is bullish, and should result in higher prices," Cramer said.

articles.title: Japan core inflation soars to highest this year as energy subsidy expiry pushes up consumer prices
articles.text:
Core inflation in Japan soared to a fresh high in 2026, coming in at 2.2% in October as higher energy costs and their knock-on effects pushed up prices in the wider economy.
Core inflation, which strips out prices of food, was lower than the 2.3% expected by Reuters-polled economists, but was higher than the 2.1% in prior month.
Headline inflation came in at 2.3% compared with September's 2.1%, while the so-called "core-core" inflation, which strips out prices of fresh food and energy, dipped slightly to 2.2% from 2.4% in the month before, government data released on Friday showed.
Energy subsidies for households expired in September, exposing consumers to higher prices brought about by the Iran war. Energy prices climbed 2.2% in October, a sharp spike from the 0.6% decline in September. Gas prices jumped 5.8% compared to the 2.4% rise the month before.
Fuel, light and water charges also saw a considerable acceleration, increasing 3.4% compared to last month's 0.8%.
Following the release, the Nikkei 225 index was down 2.1%, while the 10-year JGB yield fell 2 basis points to 2.805%.
Japan has reportedly approved reintroduction of energy subsidies in December to stave off higher imported energy prices as higher prices crimp growth, hitting consumption and net exports.
The October inflation reading is likely to push the Bank of Japan toward another rate hike in December, despite an unexpected contraction in economic growth in the third quarter. Data from LSEG indicates that there is a 72% chance of a 25 basis point hike from the Bank of Japan.
On Wednesday, BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda told parliament that the central bank was also "mindful" of the weak yen and rising crude prices, saying that these could hurt households' real income and weigh on consumption more than expected.
The yen marginally strengthened to trade at 159.59 against the dollar after the data release.
Japan's inflation is likely to still stay above 2% for the rest of 2026 and into the first quarter of 2027, according to Ma Tieying, senior economist at DBS Group Research.
She pointed out that while higher energy prices and yen weakness have contributed to headline inflation, the recent upturn is also supported by domestic factors.
"Wage growth has remained above 3% for nine consecutive months, pointing to a broader pickup in underlying inflation as stronger wage gains feed through to services prices and household spending. This suggests a more durable wage–price cycle is taking hold."
Ma expects the BOJ to raise rates in its December meeting, then twice more in 2027, bringing its terminal rate to 2%.

articles.title: Cramer says Nvidia’s woes are trumping Anthropic excitement for the rest of the AI trade
articles.text:
Nvidia's deepening sell-off following last week's leadership shake-up is overwhelming the optimism surrounding Anthropic's stock market debut and hurting the rest of the artificial intelligence trade, CNBC's Jim Cramer argued Thursday.
The Claude creator raised a record-breaking $81.3 billion, and shares surged as high as $115 in their trading debut Thursday. While off the highs of the session, the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price of $83. But the excitement did little to lift the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 both falling roughly 2%. Nvidia, once the beating heart of the AI trade, dropped 3.3% for its sixth straight day of losses — a skid that began Nov. 12, the day longtime CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation was announced amid a widening affair scandal.
Cramer argued that Nvidia's continued decline is dragging down other technology stocks, wiping out wealth faster than Anthropic's blockbuster debut can create it.
"Nvidia is casting a pall on the market that's tainting everything," the "Mad Money" host said.
Despite reporting blockbuster earnings earlier this week, with revenue more than doubling from a year earlier and beating expectations, Nvidia has struggled to regain investors' confidence in the wake of Huang's exit. Shares have fallen 16% since his resignation.
Cramer argued that Huang's desire to return could further complicate Nvidia's search for a permanent CEO. Any successor would face the challenge of leading a company still closely associated with its founder, raising questions about whether a new chief executive could establish authority while Huang remains influential. Nvidia's board said it is not considering bringing back Huang.
The continued chatter about a potential Huang return "makes it so that this still-giant company is sinking like a stone, destroying the savings of millionaires and regular index investors alike," Cramer said.
The damage extends well beyond Nvidia itself. As the longtime leader of the AI trade, the chipmaker has helped drive investor enthusiasm for everything from semiconductor manufacturers to data center infrastructure companies. Its continued decline is now weighing on those same stocks, Cramer said, cutting against the bullish hope that Anthropic's IPO would revive the rest of the AI trade.
