articles.title: Stock futures tick lower after Dow closes below 50,000 for first time since June: Live updates
articles.text:
Stock futures pulled back on Thursday night, following a horrid session on Wall Street as the much-anticipated Anthropic public market debut failed to jolt the artificial intelligence trade.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures fell 56 points, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures slipped 0.2%, and Nasdaq-100 futures shed 0.67%.
Asia-Pacific markets opened lower Friday, with South Korea's Kospi down 4.31% as heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics fell 6% and 4%, respectively. Japan's Nikkei 225 also plunged over 4%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index declined 1.43%, while mainland China's CSI 300 was flat.
The major U.S. averages fell more than 2% each in regular trading, with the Dow closing below the key 50,000 level for the first time since June.
Those steep declines came despite a strong start to the session. The Nasdaq Composite at one point traded 2.1% higher, and the S&P 500 was up as much as 1.3% on the day, as traders braced for Anthropic's first trade. But almost immediately after the Claude AI company began trading, stocks tumbled — adding to this week's already sharp losses.
Week to date, the Dow has fallen 6.2%, putting it on pace for its worst weekly performance since April 2025. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq are down 5% each, also headed for their largest one-week pullbacks in more than a year.
Yet, Deutsche Bank strategist Binky Chadha thinks the market is now "very oversold," as growth and earnings remain strong.
"The broader market, whether you look at positioning, whether you look at valuation .. we are sort of completely washed out," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell: Overtime." "It all started with a big rotation out of tech. … As the cycle has happened, we've unfortunately also gotten a lot of negative catalysts."
"That has then bled into the wider market," he said.
On Friday, traders will watch for this month's final reading of the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment report. BJ's Wholesale will also post earnings before the open.

articles.title: California attorney general issues Nvidia subpoena in probe of China chip diversion
articles.text:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia on Thursday as part of a probe of whether the company's advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China in contravention of U.S. export restrictions, his office said.
The probe comes a week after former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy. Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that is being investigation for potentially diverting restricted Nvidia chips to China.
"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," Bonta said in a statement.
"My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law," Bonta said.
"Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors," the attorney general said.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Bonta's subpoena.
Nvidia shares are down 22% in the nine trading days since Huang admitted to an extramarital affair. The stock is on pace for its seventh straight weekly loss, shedding 38% of its value over that stretch.

articles.title: Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?
articles.text:
Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a big win for the company and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.
The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
It wasn't supposed to play out this way.
Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
Some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.
Adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.
Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.
But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and said it's time to be more strategic about the trade.
Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the big indices tanked in the back half of the year.
"You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he said.
Part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.
"The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3."
While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.
Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.
"There's a reset of AI in general," said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.
Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he said, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.
Anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan said. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.
A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the company in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.
"If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he said. "There's a bigger test coming Monday."
For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.
Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.
Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.
One bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.
— CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

articles.title: Gap names new Athleta CEO, lowers full-year guidance
articles.text:
Gap Inc. on Thursday announced Ashley Kechter will be the next president and CEO of its Athleta brand, effective Dec. 14.
Kechter comes to Gap from activewear retailer Vuori, where she was global president and oversaw the brand's global business strategy, marketing and financials. She was previously global brand president of Fabletics and began her career at Gap before that.
"I'm excited to return to Gap Inc. and partner with [Gap CEO Richard Dickson] and the team to strengthen our connection with customers and shape the brand's next chapter," Kechter said in a statement.
The announcement comes after Lululemon poached former Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger to be its chief product officer last month.
"Clearly, we're disappointed with Athleta's performance, and we recognize there's a lot of work ahead," Dickson told CNBC. "We had been in rebuild mode, but now we're really in turnaround mode."
Dickson said the company is focused on getting back to its fundamentals: fabrications, feature, form, function and fit. Dickson added that Kechter will be conducting a "comprehensive review" of the brand to reposition Athleta for future success.
While the execution of its strategy has thus far "fallen short," Dickson said this new approach will allow Athleta to fully realize its potential.
Third-quarter earnings
Gap also reported mixed fiscal third-quarter earnings on Thursday and posted flat overall comparable sales. Wall Street had been expecting a comparable sales increase of 1.3%, according to StreetAccount.
Net sales grew 2%, though demand softened in October and early November due to warmer weather, the company said. Store sales increased 1%, while online sales increased 3%.
Gap also said it's recorded a $420 million adjustment to cost of goods sold and a $21 million adjustment to interest income from tariff refunds so far this year.
The company lowered its full-year net sales outlook to be "roughly flat," down from previous guidance of up between 1% and 1.5%. Gap is also now expecting adjusted earnings per share of between $2.29 and $2.34, down from an earlier expectation of between $2.35 and $2.45 per share.
Dickson said in an interview that much of the lowered guidance was due to warmer weather in the first two weeks of the quarter, but he said Gap is expecting "meaningful acceleration" in shopping ahead of the peak holiday season.
"We're monitoring the trends, and we're going to remain agile as we respond to the changing business trends," Dickson said.
Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
- Earnings per share: 82 cents adjusted vs. 78 cents expected
- Revenue: $4.01 billion vs. $4.02 billion expected
For the quarter, Gap reported net income of $311 million, or 86 cents per share, compared with $236 million, or 62 cents per share, the year prior. Sales rose slightly from $3.94 billion the year prior.
Brand sales
At Athleta, net sales were down 14% compared with last year, coming in at $220 million. Comparable sales for the banner sank 15%, which the company attributed to "limited traction" from efforts to modernize its merchandise and marketing.
The company's namesake brand saw 9% comparable sales growth for the quarter, with net sales of $1.1 billion, marking an 11% increase compared with last year. Dickson said it was the brand's 12th consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales.
"Gap is really firing on all cylinders, and the consistency of the brand is really giving us confidence in the brand's ability to continue its momentum," Dickson said.
The Old Navy banner saw flat comparable sales for the quarter and net sales of $2.3 billion, up 1% compared with last year. It's the first earnings report since the brand, which has been experiencing sluggish sales, named Michael Francis as its new CEO last quarter. Francis began his role at Old Navy on Nov. 2.
Banana Republic saw its net sales sink 3% compared with last year, which the company attributed to delayed demand for cold-weather categories and a women's fall assortment that fell flat. Wall Street had been expecting growth of 1.5%, according to StreetAccount.
Dickson said the brand has since introduced new products and seen demand "rebound" as cooler weather has set in across the country.
"We've been encouraged by the early customer response, and we should see sequential improvement in the fourth quarter," he said. "There's some work to do here, but with peak selling still ahead, I'm confident that the team is focused on the right areas and [will] ultimately position Banana well for growth."

articles.title: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
articles.text:
Tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock. The deal is set to close in early 2027, according to a statement.
The sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses. Five years later, the software maker is unloading the email-marketing company for less than one-third of that price after Mailchimp became a drag on its overall revenue growth.
The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset. The company bought productivity software startup Airtable in September for 10% of what it was once worth.
The Bending Spoons portfolio also contains AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.
In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment. The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, said at a September company briefing.
Also on Thursday, Intuit announced stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The company reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue.
While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.
Management called for $22.88 to $23.12 in adjusted earnings per share for the 2027 fiscal year, with $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $23.62 in adjusted earnings per share on $23.43 billion in revenue. Intuit shares tumbled 15% in extended trading.
The company said Mailchimp should produce $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue, which would be down 1% to flat year over year. In August Aujla said Intuit anticipated Mailchimp's higher effective prices offsetting increased client churn. Mailchimp was founded in 2001. Rivals include Klaviyo, which went public in 2023.
Berkshire Hathaway invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the acquirer went public in July, and in October Bending Spoons said Berkshire invested another $330 million.

articles.title: Congress passes bill to protect older investors from financial fraud
articles.text:
Bipartisan legislation aimed at protecting older Americans and other vulnerable adults from financial fraud has cleared Congress, putting it on track to become law.
Called the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act of 2025 and passed by the House in June, H.R. 2478 was approved by unanimous consent in the Senate Wednesday night — meaning no senators objected to its passage.
The measure will next head to President Donald Trump's desk. The White House did not respond to a CNBC request for comment on whether Trump plans to sign the bill into law.
The bill would generally allow mutual fund companies and their transfer agents, which handle shareholder records and transactions, to temporarily delay paying out redemption requests when they suspect an older or otherwise vulnerable investor is being financially exploited.
"Financial exploitation can have devastating consequences for victims and their families," said Erin Koeppel, a managing director and government relations and public policy counsel at the CFP Board, the organization that oversees the certified financial planner certification. "This legislation fills an important regulatory gap that can help protect vulnerable investors before assets are lost."
Reported fraud among older adults hit $3 billion in 2025
The measure's congressional approval comes amid growing financial fraud among older Americans. Those age 60 or older reported losing about $3 billion to fraud in 2025, a 25% increase from $2.4 billion in 2024, according to the Federal Trade Commission's latest report to Congress on fraud among older adults, which was released in October. That amount is 400% higher than the $600 million reported lost in 2020.
"Generally, we support all legislation that aims to prevent any form of financial elder abuse," said Bob Blancato, national coordinator for the Elder Justice Coalition, an advocacy group.
While just 6% of older fraud victims reported losing $100,000 or more in 2025, those losses accounted for 70% of the age group's total reported losses. The number of people reporting losses of that magnitude rose nearly sixfold to 6,769 in 2025, from 1,136 in 2020.
However, because many scams go unreported, the FTC estimates actual losses in 2025 could have been anywhere from $13.3 billion to $119.5 billion. In 2024, the estimated range was from $10.1 billion to $81.5 billion.
Scammers are increasingly targeting Americans' life savings by impersonating banks, businesses and government agencies, according to the FTC. The schemes often involve fabricated emergencies that convince victims to transfer money to supposedly protect their accounts from being compromised.
Additionally, content created by artificial intelligence that can help criminals carry out schemes is becoming increasingly difficult to detect and easier to make, according to the FBI.
What the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act does
Under the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act, mutual fund companies and their transfer agents could temporarily postpone payments when they reasonably believe a redemption request involves financial exploitation.
This would apply to investors age 65 and older, as well as younger adults reasonably believed to have a mental or physical impairment that prevents them from protecting their own interests.
Companies could initially delay paying out redemption proceeds for up to 15 business days. They could extend the hold by another 10 business days if they still reasonably believe exploitation already occurred, is underway or was attempted. State regulators, certain government agencies or courts could also extend the hold.
How a 'trusted contact' may help thwart fraud
The bill also addresses the use of a "trusted contact" — an individual whom financial firms can contact when concerns arise about an investor's account. That person may be able to intervene to prevent the fraud by reaching out to the account holder.
Mutual fund companies that opt into the new protections would be required to ask customers to provide the name and contact information of at least one trusted contact.
The legislation would build on existing investor protections. Already, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, or FINRA, permits brokerage firms to temporarily place holds on certain transactions if they suspect financial exploitation of an older or otherwise vulnerable investor.
Additionally, FINRA requires brokerages to make a reasonable effort to add a trusted contact to accounts, although investors are not required to provide one. Many banks and other financial institutions also ask account holders for a trusted contact.
Taxes paid on some fraud targeted in separate bill
Separately, another House-passed bipartisan bill that aims to provide some relief for certain scam victims is awaiting action in the Senate. That measure, the Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act, is intended to prevent people who lose money to scams from suffering additional financial harm through the federal tax system.
The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 temporarily limited deductions for personal theft losses, and Trump's "big beautiful bill" of 2025 made those limits permanent. Some investment scam losses may still be deductible, but losses from some romance and impersonation scams generally aren't, according to a 2025 IRS memo. Victims who withdraw money from a traditional 401(k) or IRA may also owe income tax on the withdrawal and, if they're under 59½, possibly a 10% early-withdrawal penalty.
The Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act, H.R. 9500, would repeal those deduction limits and waive the 10% penalty on withdrawals tied to deductible fraud losses. The House passed it 408-17 in September, and it was referred to the Senate Finance Committee. It's unclear whether the Senate will take it up before this Congress ends.
"We would hope ... the Senate will join the House in passing H.R. 9500 to end another form of elder financial abuse," Blancato said.

articles.title: What Ron Johnson's 'Ponzi scheme' label gets wrong about Social Security, experts say
articles.text:
A new Senate budget committee hearing on Wednesday reignited an old Social Security question: Is the program, which provides monthly benefits to millions of Americans, a Ponzi scheme?
Senate Budget Committee Chairman Ron Johnson, a Republican representing Wisconsin, called Social Security "a legal Ponzi scheme" in his opening remarks. But experts say his comments overlook how Social Security works and the real dilemma for lawmakers over its looming funding shortfall.
A Ponzi scheme is an investment fraud that uses funds from new investors to pay existing investors, according to the Securities and Exchange Commission, Johnson wrote in his chairman's hearing memo. He said that Social Security fits the description if you remove the word "fraud."
Johnson's comments followed his Wednesday morning interview on Fox Business, where he said, "At this point, there's really no way to fix Social Security."
"You can't fix it, you just shut it down and then hope that you can recover some of your money," Johnson said during the Fox Business interview.
"As far as I can tell, this is the first time in decades that a senior senator, chairman of the budget committee, said he would rather shut down Social Security than fix it," Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., said during the hearing.
At the Senate hearing, Johnson said his comments during the TV interview were "imprecise" and that he was talking broadly about Ponzi schemes, not Social Security, that need to be shut down.
Johnson said he wants lawmakers to pass a law to ensure seniors' Social Security benefits are not reduced, "then roll up our sleeves and fix the real problem, which is $24 trillion of 10-year deficits."
The Congressional Budget Office has projected a $24.4 trillion cumulative federal budget deficit over the next 10 years.
Johnson proposed a bill on Wednesday that would allow for Social Security retirement benefits to be funded by general revenue once that trust fund reaches its insolvency date.
Critics say that's not a viable solution. Using the general fund to pay for Social Security would "absolutely explode the national debt" and cost 165% of gross domestic product over 75 years, Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, a nonpartisan organization, said in a statement.
Social Security 'runs on its own budget'
The way Johnson described the program during the hearing was "out of touch with the way the American public understands and knows Social Security," said Bill Sweeney, senior vice president of government affairs at AARP, a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization representing Americans age 50 and over.
"The budget committee should know that Social Security is not part of the budget," Sweeney said. "It runs on its own budget."
Social Security does affect the unified federal deficit and debt held by the public when outlays exceed dedicated revenues, according to CBO. The Treasury securities held by Social Security's trust funds count as intragovernmental debt, which is included in gross federal debt but not in debt held by the public.
Social Security benefits are mainly funded by payroll tax contributions. When the program's income exceeds its costs, the surplus is invested in special U.S. Treasury securities held in the trust funds.
Social Security is not allowed to borrow money and cannot go into debt, according to Sweeney.
"It's never contributed a penny to the debt," Sweeney said. "It's not part of the national debt because it's in a separate budget."
Social Security's funding challenge
Social Security's trust funds may be depleted within the next six to eight years, based on current projections. If that happens, Social Security benefits may be cut.
In six years — the fourth quarter of 2032 — the Social Security retirement trust fund may run out, Social Security's trustees projected in June. At that time, 78% of those benefits would be payable.
In eight years — the third quarter of 2034 — Social Security's combined retirement and disability trust funds may run out, when 83% of scheduled benefits would be payable, according to the Social Security trustees' projections.
Had payroll tax revenue kept up with gross domestic product over the past four decades, the program would be able to pay full benefits until 2059 — an additional 25 years versus current projections, according to recent AARP research.
At the hearing, Johnson held up a picture of the trust funds, which he said is a "four-drawer file in Parkersburg, West Virginia."
Johnson similarly mentioned the trust fund files at a July 2023 hearing. In 2005, then-President George W. Bush was shown paper evidence of Social Security's U.S. bonds during a visit to the Bureau of Public Debt in Parkersburg.
While the politicians' actions seem to suggest the trust funds aren't real, experts say they are legitimate.
"It's all about trying to scare people into thinking that Social Security is not going to be there for you when it's time for you to retire," Sweeney said. "For 91 years it has been, and there's no reason to believe it won't be."
Wednesday's Senate hearing was a "missed opportunity" for a more in-depth discussion of the challenges facing Social Security, said Jason Fichtner, a witness at the hearing and executive director of the LIMRA Retirement Income Institute, a research initiative within the insurance trade association LIMRA.
Plans such as raising or eliminating the taxable maximum for payroll contributions to Social Security may push the program's funding woes 20 or 30 years later, but would not make the program solvent for the 75-year target, according to Fichtner, a former Social Security Administration official.
Moreover, fixing Social Security would not resolve the government's larger fiscal issues, which would still leave the economy vulnerable to bond market strain, he said.
"The other issue is fear," Fichtner said. "We do see evidence now of people claiming Social Security earlier because of their fear of the trust funds running out of money or Social Security not being able to pay benefits."
A June 2025 AARP survey found 49% of respondents who had recently claimed or planned to claim Social Security benefits earlier than planned were mostly motivated by concerns the program may run out of money.
"Social Security is very effective at solving problems, and it's a thorn in the side of the federal government because they have done a horrible job managing so many aspects of our finances," said labor economist Kathryn Anne Edwards, a witness at the hearing and a senior fellow at the National Academy of Social Insurance, a provider of research and policy analysis on social insurance and economic security programs.
"But Americans don't see it that way," she said.
More than half of Social Security recipients surveyed say benefits are their main source of income, according to an August AARP poll.
Social Security reform provides an opportunity to expand the program to help meet Americans' needs, Edwards said. Adding universal paid family and medical leave to the program could help individuals and families who don't currently have access to those benefits, she said. Moreover, strengthening unemployment insurance could help ensure financial security amid the prospect of AI-related job losses, Edwards said.
Senators who were elected on Nov. 3 will be in office when the retirement trust fund depletion date hits in 2032. The next session of Congress may provide an opportunity for "serious" hearings on the future of Social Security, Sweeney said.
The Senate budget committee's Wednesday hearing followed other recent hearings on the program's future, including a June Senate finance subcommittee hearing and an August Senate finance full committee hearing.

articles.title: 3-step method to influence people and win them over, from a Stanford expert: ‘Your voice is like a muscle’
articles.text:
Think back on the most memorable, inspiring speeches or presentations you've witnessed. They probably weren't delivered in a monotone, Matt Abrahams says.
"The human brain is designed to pick out and focus on things that are novel and new," says Abrahams, a Stanford University lecturer on strategic communication and host of the "Think Fast, Talk Smart" podcast. "So anything that stays the same, like a monotonous voice or cadence, we don't pay as much attention to."
Indeed, successful leaders often have an uncanny ability to win over a crowd: The power of persuasion lies not just in what you actually have to say, but also in how you say it, research shows. The topic has taken on new relevance this week as Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress steps into one of the most closely watched leadership roles in corporate America.
In appearances this week, including Nvidia's quarterly earnings call and an interview with CNBC's "Mad Money" host Jim Cramer, Kress has discussed the company's performance. She's also addressed employees and investors in a time of leadership upheaval, following Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang's high-profile resignation on Nov. 12.
How Kress communicates has drawn attention and, in some circles, criticism. On Wednesday, The Wall Street Journal described her public speaking style as "slow, steady, almost monotone." That doesn't necessarily make it ineffective. Her situation, however, highlights a broader challenge leaders face when they need to inform, reassure and persuade large groups of people at once.
Generally speaking, anyone can stand a better chance at persuading others to follow them by honing an engaging speaking style, says Abrahams. Some people may be naturally expressive and engaging. For others, it's a skill that requires time and practice.
Abrahams suggests a three-step playbook for anyone learning to speak more persuasively: "repetition, reflection and feedback."
3 steps to influence people with your voice: 'Repetition, reflection and feedback'
Abrahams' simplest advice for making yourself a more engaging speaker: "When you're using emotive words, reflect the emotion in them." That means adding some emphasis to words like "exciting," "huge" or "challenging," and so on. If you tend to speak monotonously, leaning into obviously emotive words can help you vary your tone and inflection enough to keep your audience's attention.
There's a catch, of course: People find inauthenticity off-putting and disingenuous, says Abrahams. Don't alter your voice entirely, he suggests — just add some variety to your intonation and speaking volume. Learning to do so while still sounding natural takes practice, he notes.
"Your voice is like a muscle," says Abrahams. "You can train it. You can grow it [and] strengthen it, just like you go to the gym to lift weights."
Practicing repetition starts with reading aloud from a chosen text, which Abrahams recommends so you don't have to overthink what you're saying. And the same way you might lift heavy weights to get stronger, Abrahams suggests reading overly expressive material to start getting out of your comfort zone and practice being energetic and engaging. He instructs his Stanford students to try reading Dr. Seuss books, as their playful words and bouncy rhymes can naturally make for a lively performance.
While practicing reading out loud, record yourself to watch and listen to later, Abrahams recommends. Then, use the recording to reflect on what works and what doesn't, and incorporate your self-feedback into your next reading. You can also play the recording for a few trusted peers to get their thoughts, Abrahams says.
If a line reading doesn't sound natural in your voice, feels flat or even rushed, keep trying it until you're satisfied, he says. Leaders are often asked to deliver lengthy speeches or talk for long periods in interviews and panels, so it's important to build your vocal stamina, he adds.
"We have to calibrate ourselves," he says.
Abrahams asks his Stanford graduate students to review their recordings in three ways, he says:
- With no sound, so they can focus on their physical presence
- With sound only, so they can dissect their vocal delivery
- All together, to review the full performance
"That's how you train your brain to see: 'What do I need to sound like?'" says Abrahams.

articles.title: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
articles.text:
The subagency of the Commerce Department that regulates and enforces exports approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, according to documents released Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee.
Some of those approvals, made by Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, included sales to companies designated by the Department of Defense as "Chinese Military Companies," according to the documents. From December through May, companies had made 3.4 million requests for sales of U.S. AI chips to China, the committee reported, citing those made by Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices.
"Over the past month, the administration's handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk. The Bureau of Industry and Security has failed to enforce the rules, and Congress must now conduct rigorous oversight of the administration's policies," Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said at a meeting of the panel Thursday at which members voted to release the documents.
Spokespersons for Nvidia and AMD said their companies comply with U.S. export control laws.
Nvidia argued it was following the Commerce Department regulations that were in effect at the time.
A spokesperson from the Bureau of Industry and Security said it shared information with Congress on both approvals and denials of licenses for Nvidia's H200 and comparable chips. "Licensing decisions are the product of deliberation and consultation among multiple U.S. Government agencies," the spokesperson said.
"The review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes. Despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China," Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo told CNBC.
On Tuesday, Nvidia reported $2.4 billion in quarterly revenue from H200 and related chip sales in China. In total, customers based in China and Hong Kong made up about 9.5% of all revenue.
"AMD complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations," AMD said through a spokesperson.
The approval of 879,000 AI chips is "not that many," Bernstein Senior Analyst Stacy Rasgon told CNBC, adding that this news is not surprising.
"It doesn't sound to me like they're approving everything they got willy nilly," Rasgon said of the Commerce Department. With 879,000 approvals out of 3.4 million requested AI chip sales, he added, "There was a process in place, and it sounds like they approved about one out of every four."
Despite a rapid succession of China export controls on AI chips that started under the Biden administration in 2022, Nvidia and AMD both re-engineered some chips to comply and be sold legally in China. And in December, Trump said Nvidia could ship H200s, its older generation Hopper chips, to "approved customers in China" if the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales.
The U.S. then licensed Nvidia H200 sales to Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese companies, although sales were limited because Beijing didn't approve large-scale imports, chip analyst Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy told CNBC last week.
H200 sales numbers remained low due to those restrictions on China's end. Nvidia said H200 shipments to China made up less than 1% of data center revenue for the quarter that ended in July.
"In the grand context of the size of this market and how much they're shipping, it's a rounding error. It's tiny," Rasgon told CNBC.
The committee cited the Export Control Reform Act as justification for releasing the data. The panel said the law allows it to declassify and release export data if it "determines that the withholding of the following information is contrary to the national interest."
The license requests released by the Foreign Affairs Committee include requests to sell to major firms including ByteDance, Tesla (Shanghai) and Baidu.
The release of documents comes in the wake of Jensen Huang's resignation from the chip supplier Nvidia after news surfaced that he had several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy that led to concerns about Nvidia chips being diverted to China.
In the weeks since, Republicans and Democrats in Congress have called for legislation to be passed that would impose stricter export controls on the sale of advanced AI chips to China and other adversaries.
"The license information we are disclosing today will help inform the American public about how BIS has handled licenses for Nvidia H200 and equivalent AMD chips to China. The public has the right to know how these decisions were made," Meeks said.
Mast said two of the firms listed in Nvidia license applications to BIS — Maginfra and New Matrix — are suspected "smuggling fronts." The New York Times reported in November that both companies had empty offices and had ties to companies under national security sanctions.
"Both are fake companies. If BIS approved the sale of these chips to these firms, obviously that is of tremendous concern to us — especially given that President Trump made clear last year that the sale of any AI chips to China will have very real national security conditions," Mast said at the Thursday meeting.
Maginfra and New Matrix did not reply to requests for comment.
Shares of AMD fell Thursday after the investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging the company "has its own China problem." The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers."
CNBC did not independently verify this information.
Fallout from the Huang scandal on Capitol Hill has intensified in the last week, as lawmakers question the degree to which the former head of Nvidia's relationship with the suspected Chinese spy could have jeopardized national security and American AI dominance.
Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels Dec. 2.
Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., announced on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also agreed to testify.
Lutnick has come under fire over his relationship to Huang and for his failure to take action on Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Alice Huang, with whom the former Nvidia CEO had an affair, was an executive until 2025. U.S. investigators suspect Megaspeed diverted Nvidia chips to China.
Amid that criticism, the Commerce Department on Monday issued an interim final rule to close a loophole that has allowed Chinese companies to lease Nvidia's advancing computing power from data centers in third countries.
The rule was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release.
— Megan Cassella, Daren Fonda and Kif Leswing contributed to this report.

articles.title: S&P 500 heads for 6th straight decline. Plus, J&J advances two key products
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch — an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. Markets fell on Thursday, putting the S & P 500 on pace for its sixth straight session of declines. The index has now dropped roughly 7% from its Oct. 6 record close of 7,818.93. The beginning of the market decline Thursday lined up closely to Anthropic's first trade. The frontier lab opened trading at $111.50 per share, a 34% pop from its $83 IPO price. But the early enthusiasm quickly faded. As Anthropic fell from its initial burst and dropped below $100 per share, it brought down the rest of the AI theme with it. A silver lining to the recent sell-off is that the S & P Oscillator finally moved into oversold territory following Wednesday's drop, prompting us to make a few buys that took our cash position down to a still-healthy 15.5% from over 16%. We added to Meta, FedEx Freight and later Constellation Brands . One of the few bright spots in the market on Thursday was cybersecurity stocks. Palo Alto Networks reported an excellent quarter Wednesday evening, beating and raising all key metrics. The cybersecurity theme was reinforced Thursday after JPMorgan Chase said some of its third-party service providers were targeted in a cyberattack. Having the best and the most up to date cybersecurity solutions is extremely important in the AI age, and we continue to believe Palo Alto Networks and fellow Club holding CrowdStrike are the two best-of-breed names in the industry. Johnson & Johnson is back again this week with two more encouraging developments. Starting with Ottava, the healthcare giant announced Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center in Houston will become the first hospital to commercially install its robotic surgical system. The hospital was involved in the clinical trials for Ottava, which in July was authorized by the Food and Drug Administration for use in 10 general surgery procedures involving the upper abdomen. J & J is betting on Ottava's sleek design , smaller footprint and other innovative features to help it win market share in the robotic surgery market, which has long been dominated by Intuitive Surgical . Ottava shouldn't be looked at as a near-term needle-mover, but rather a multiyear play that adds to growth later in the decade and beyond. Separately, J & J also submitted its antipsychotic drug Caplyta to the FDA for approval to treat bipolar mania, or manic episodes associated with bipolar I disorder. The move from J & J follows two positive late-stage studies that showed Caplyta significantly reduced manic symptoms compared with a placebo as early as the third day, with improvements sustained through the third week. Caplyta is already the first and only FDA-approved medication to treat depressive episodes associated with both bipolar I and bipolar II disorder in adults, either on its own or alongside certain other medications. The drug is also approved to treat schizophrenia, and as an add-on therapy for major depressive disorder. If cleared for bipolar mania, it would mark Caplyta's fifth approved use in adults. In the third quarter, Caplyta revenue rose 66% from the year-ago period to $398 million and crossed over $1 billion in sales for 2026. That makes it one of the fastest-growing drugs in J & J's portfolio. J & J shares have not responded to the positive news, as the rotation into healthcare stocks lost some steam this week. Shares have dropped about 7% from Friday's record close. But this is a name we want to keep owning for its pharma growth, and as a way to keep the portfolio diversified beyond just AI names. After the closing bell on Thursday, Gap , Intuit , Ross Stores , and Elastic report quarterly earnings. The CEOs of Gap and Intuit will join Jim on "Mad Money" tonight. We'll also monitoring Ross for insights into the competitive dynamics versus Club name TJX , which took a welcome step forward in its own earnings report Wednesday. BJ's Wholesale , a rival of Costco, reports before the opening bell on Friday. On the data side, we'll see University of Michigan consumer sentiment and inflation expectations. articles.title: The stock market could be headed for more turbulence. How one investor is preparing
articles.text: (See the video above for Todd's complete chart breakdown.) Normally I use this weekly column to walk through the individual stocks we're adding, holding or cutting in our portfolios at Inside Edge Capital. This week I'm stepping back to the big picture. That's where the risk is right now. Between the geopolitical noise, the domestic political drama, some genuinely strange ghost-in-the-machine stuff, and Nvidia's blowout quarter amid its leadership transition, the indexes are trading almost schizophrenically. And they're sitting right at the edge of key support. If that gives way, it could open up a fresh wave of selling. Yesterday we rebalanced our Tactical Alpha Growth portfolio for the fifth time since October. We've been in business for five years, and this is by far our most active six-week stretch. We cut net equity exposure from 92% to 70%, raised cash to 20% in T-bills, and added a 5% hedge with an inverse Nasdaq 100 ETF. Here are the exact sector changes we shared with our clients. Beyond the worries over massive AI buildout spending, we're watching interest rates that just won't quit. The outlook now calls for at least three more Fed hikes over the next four months. Zoom out to the longest trend, and the 10-year TIPS yield tracks the value-to-growth ratio. Real yields are at 2.87%, the high end of the last decade, and the value-to-growth ratio is pressing against the top of the range it's held all year. If that blue line breaks out, value could continue to outperform growth. That's an uncomfortable spot in the middle of the AI revolution, and yesterday's moves position us for it. Of course, our portfolios, and probably yours, are sitting on nice gains in semiconductors. Selling those and writing a big check to the IRS next year isn't very appealing. So instead of dumping winners, we hedged growth with a 5% position in PSQ, the ProShares Short QQQ. The QQQ chart below lays out the levels. The $655 zone is the line in the sand. Below it there's a little air pocket down to about $635, the area that capped the market in the fourth quarter of 2025 and again in the first quarter of 2026. If we test $635 and it can't hold, I plan to add to the PSQ hedge. That's not a prediction. It's just a hard look at where things stand right now. If the market pulls itself together and holds $655, I'll close the hedge quickly, figure out where leadership is coming from based on sector rotation, and put the cash back to work. If your head is spinning, you're not alone. That's the kind of market we're in, and for active managers, this is when the tough get going. Todd Gordon is the founder of Inside Edge Capital, LLC . articles.title: Không phải nước sôi để qua đêm, đây mới là 3 loại "nước độc" gây ung thư nhưng đội lốt lành mạnh
articles.text:
Không phải nước sôi để qua đêm, đây mới là 3 loại "nước độc" gây ung thư nhưng đội lốt lành mạnh
Nhiều người ám ảnh chuyện nước để qua đêm sinh độc mà vô tư uống hằng ngày 3 loại nước tưởng chừng bổ dưỡng nhưng lại âm thầm làm tăng nguy cơ ung thư.
Trong thói quen sinh hoạt hằng ngày, không ít người kiêng tuyệt đối nước đun sôi để qua đêm hay nước đun lại nhiều lần vì lo ngại chất nitrit gây ung thư. Tuy nhiên, Phó giáo sư Phạm Chí Hồng (Fan Zhihong) thuộc Khoa Dinh dưỡng và An toàn thực phẩm tại Đại học Nông nghiệp Trung Quốc (Trung Quốc) khẳng định đây là sự hiểu lầm phổ biến.
Theo chuyên gia, nitrit chỉ hình thành khi có nguồn nitrat dồi dào, trong khi nước tinh khiết hay nước máy đạt chuẩn gần như không tạo ra lượng độc chất đáng kể dù để qua đêm. Các thử nghiệm thực tế cho thấy ngay cả khi đun sôi nước liên tục 20 lần, hàm lượng nitrit đo được chỉ ở mức 0,038mg/L, thấp hơn rất nhiều so với ngưỡng gây hại cho cơ thể. Đáng lo ngại hơn cả là 3 loại đồ uống thường được gắn mác "tốt cho sức khỏe" dưới đây nhưng nếu lạm dụng sai cách lại âm thầm tiếp tay cho ung thư.
1. Nước nóng trên 65 độ C
Nhiều người tin rằng uống trà nóng, nước đun sôi còn bốc khói hay húp canh nóng hổi giúp giữ ấm cơ thể và tốt cho tiêu hóa. Thế nhưng, Cơ quan Nghiên cứu Ung thư Quốc tế (IARC) trực thuộc Tổ chức Y tế Thế giới (WHO) đã xếp đồ uống có nhiệt độ trên 65 độ C vào Nhóm 2A, tức nhóm tác nhân có khả năng cao gây ung thư cho con người, cùng nhóm với khói đốt củi hay thịt đỏ.
Theo phân tích của Phó giáo sư Phạm Chí Hồng, niêm mạc thực quản và dạ dày chỉ chịu được mức nhiệt khoảng 40 đến 50 độ C. Khi thường xuyên tiếp xúc với nước nóng trên 65 độ C, lớp màng nhầy bảo vệ bị phá hủy, gây bỏng nhiệt lặp đi lặp lại ở các mô đáy. Để tự sửa chữa, tế bào biểu mô phải liên tục phân chia trong môi trường viêm mạn tính, sản sinh gốc tự do làm đứt gãy chuỗi DNA và kích hoạt đột biến gen ác tính. Một nghiên cứu công bố trên tạp chí y khoa BMJ khảo sát 48.582 người tại Golestan (Iran) ghi nhận nhóm uống trà từ 65 độ C trở lên đối mặt với nguy cơ ung thư biểu mô tế bào vảy thực quản tăng vọt.
2. Nước ép trái cây tách xơ, nhiều đường
Nước ép hoa quả thường được xem là thức uống "healthy" giúp bổ sung vitamin và thanh lọc cơ thể. Tuy nhiên, quá trình ép lấy nước và lọc bỏ hoàn toàn bã xơ đã biến loại nước này thành dung dịch đậm đặc đường tự do, đặc biệt là đường fructose.
Nghiên cứu dịch tễ học quy mô lớn NutriNet Santé tại Pháp theo dõi hơn 100.000 người trưởng thành và đăng tải trên tạp chí BMJ chỉ ra rằng việc tiêu thụ thường xuyên đồ uống có đường, bao gồm cả nước ép trái cây nguyên chất, làm tăng nguy cơ mắc ung thư tổng thể, đặc biệt là ung thư vú. Khi thiếu vắng chất xơ làm chậm quá trình hấp thu, lượng đường lớn đi thẳng vào gan và máu gây tăng đột biến đường huyết cùng nồng độ insulin. Tình trạng này thúc đẩy phản ứng viêm toàn thân, tích tụ mỡ nội tạng và tạo môi trường chuyển hóa thuận lợi cho tế bào ác tính phát triển.
3. Trà pha quá đặc
Trà vốn giàu polyphenol chống oxy hóa tốt cho sức khỏe, nhưng thói quen hãm trà đặc quánh và uống thay nước lọc mỗi ngày lại biến thức uống này thành gánh nặng cho đường tiêu hóa. Các nghiên cứu dịch tễ học đăng tải trên tạp chí International Journal of Cancer và American Journal of Clinical Nutrition từng ghi nhận mối liên hệ giữa việc tiêu thụ trà quá đặc kéo dài với sự gia tăng nguy cơ tổn thương niêm mạc đường tiêu hóa trên và ung thư dạ dày.
Nguyên nhân là do trà pha quá đặc chứa nồng độ cao tanin, caffein và hoạt chất alkaloid dễ gây kích ứng mạnh, làm co thắt mạch máu niêm mạc và bào mòn lớp chất nhầy bảo vệ dạ dày. Khi hàng rào niêm mạc bị viêm loét kéo dài, dạ dày trở nên nhạy cảm hơn trước sự tấn công của vi khuẩn Helicobacter pylori cùng các chất sinh ung thư từ thực phẩm. Hơn nữa, trà đặc thường được uống ngay khi vừa pha ở nhiệt độ rất cao, tạo ra tác động kép vừa bỏng nhiệt vừa ăn mòn niêm mạc, đồng thời lượng oxalat dồi dào trong trà đặc còn làm tăng nguy cơ kết tủa sỏi thận.
Uống nước thế nào để bảo vệ cơ thể?
Để việc uống nước hằng ngày thực sự nuôi dưỡng sức khỏe thay vì vô tình làm tổn thương nội tạng, Phó giáo sư Phạm khuyến nghị bạn nên duy trì những nguyên tắc sau:
- Ưu tiên nước lọc ấm ở mức 20 đến 40 độ C: Đây là ngưỡng nhiệt độ êm dịu nhất với niêm mạc thực quản và dạ dày. Nếu uống trà hoặc canh nóng, hãy chờ nguội bớt dưới 60 độ C mới thưởng thức.
- Chia nhỏ lượng nước và uống rải rác cả ngày: Duy trì khoảng 1,5 đến 2 lít nước mỗi ngày tùy theo thể trạng, uống chậm từng ngụm nhỏ thay vì đợi khát mới uống dồn dập một lúc gây áp lực cho thận và rối loạn điện giải.
- Nắm bắt các thời điểm vàng: Uống một ly nước ấm ngay sau khi thức dậy giúp đánh thức hệ tiêu hóa và hỗ trợ tuần hoàn; uống trước bữa ăn khoảng 30 phút giúp dạ dày chuẩn bị tốt hơn cho quá trình tiêu hóa.
- Không dùng trà đặc hay nước ép thay nước lọc: Hạn chế uống trà đặc khi bụng đói, ưu tiên ăn trái cây nguyên quả để giữ trọn chất xơ và tránh uống quá nhiều nước sát giờ đi ngủ để không làm gián đoạn giấc ngủ.

articles.title: This tech stock has been nearly cut in half this year. I think Wall Street is getting it wrong
articles.text: Today I'm looking at a company with one of the coolest names in tech: AppLovin . The Palo Alto, California-based company operates an AI-driven digital advertising platform that helps businesses reach customers and mobile app developers make money from ads. Its AXON technology matches advertisers with potential customers to boost the effectiveness of their campaigns. Key points Revenue growth is accelerating again. AppLovin's AI technology could help it fend off disruption and expand into e-commerce. Exceptionally high profit margins and strong cash flow are fueling aggressive share buybacks. I've long believed digital advertising is one of the best business models in technology. Just look at the success of Meta and Google. The stock has come under considerable pressure, falling roughly 46% from its 52-week high. Part of the concern has been that advances in AI could disrupt AppLovin's advertising business, potentially allowing competitors or advertisers to bypass its platform. But I see AI as an opportunity for AppLovin, not just a threat. The company is already using AI to improve advertising performance, and that advantage could help it win more businesses as it expands into e-commerce. Why I'm buying Revenue growth is picking up speed In the second quarter, revenue growth decelerated to 53% year over year. For most companies, that would be an extraordinary number. But for AppLovin, it was enough to raise concerns that its best days were behind it. Fast-forward 90 days, and the company reported third-quarter revenue of $2.18 billion , up 55% from a year earlier and ahead of Wall Street's expectations. Net revenue per installation increased 55%, while installation volume grew just 2%. That tells me AppLovin's AI models are becoming more effective, allowing advertisers to generate better results and pay more for those outcomes. E-commerce opens up a new market Advertisers are increasingly using AppLovin's technology to reach potential customers, creating an entirely new growth opportunity beyond mobile games. Consumer advertiser spending grew at a triple-digit rate from a year earlier and increased by double digits from the previous quarter. Wall Street is expecting revenue growth of roughly 25% in 2027. I'm modeling 30%, in line with management's long-term growth target, and I think there's potential to do even better as e-commerce gains traction. Exceptional profitability supports aggressive buybacks In the third quarter, AppLovin reported a net income margin of 66%. To put that in perspective, the typical S & P 500 company generates a net margin closer to 10% to 15%. AppLovin's adjusted EBITDA margin was even higher, at 84%. APP YTD mountain AppLovin Corporation, YTD Those margins translate into enormous cash generation. The company produced approximately $1.4 billion in free cash flow during the quarter, giving it plenty of flexibility to reinvest in its business and return capital to shareholders. Management is doing just that. AppLovin repurchased shares aggressively during the quarter, at an average price of roughly $341, and its board expanded its buyback authorization by $3.2 billion. Why now? Despite the recent rebound, there's still meaningful upside as AppLovin's growth accelerates. There's also been a positive development on the regulatory front. The SEC has reportedly closed its inquiry into AppLovin's data-collection practices without recommending enforcement action, which removes a source of uncertainty for investors. My 12-month price target is $545, based on a blend of earnings and EBITDA valuations. That represents roughly 39% upside from the stock's current price of $393. Bottom line AppLovin's AI models need to keep improving, and its expansion beyond gaming is still pretty new. But I believe the company can turn AI disruption into an advantage. Combined with accelerating revenue growth and aggressive share repurchases, that makes this one of the more compelling opportunities I see in technology right now. Paul Meeks is the Managing Director and Head of Technology Research of Freedom Capital Markets . Disclosures: Meeks does not own shares personally or through the firm. articles.title: MXH đang hóng tin cặp đôi nữ Chủ tịch - tài tử ly hôn vì đàng trai ngoại tình với đại gia 1 đời chồng
articles.text:
MXH đang hóng tin cặp đôi nữ Chủ tịch - tài tử ly hôn vì đàng trai ngoại tình với đại gia 1 đời chồng
Công chúng lo lắng cho cậu con trai mới 2 tuổi của cặp đôi vàng showbiz.
Cuộc hôn nhân của nữ ca sĩ kiêm CEO New Napassorn và tài tử Peck Premmanat đã liên tục khiến dư luận Thái Lan nổi sóng trong vài tháng qua. Mọi chuyện khởi nguồn từ tháng 8 năm nay khi Peck Premmanat bất ngờ vướng tin phản bội bà xã, cặp kè với nữ đại gia 1 đời chồng. Tới nay, tờ Khaosod cho hay, New Napassorn - Peck Premmanat lại vừa dính nghi vấn rạn nứt, ly hôn.
Thông tin này đã khiến cho công chúng Thái Lan hoang mang, dậy sóng, bởi lẽ New Napassorn - Peck Premmanat từ lâu đã được xem là cặp đôi vàng ở Tbiz.
Trong diễn biến mới nhất, Peck - New vừa cùng nhau xuất hiện trong sự kiện khai trương 1 cửa hàng ngay giữa tin đồn chia tay, tại đây họ đã thẳng thắn lên tiếng làm rõ mọi chuyện. Theo đó, cặp đôi đã mạnh mẽ bác bỏ nghi vấn rạn nứt hôn nhân, đồng thời cho biết khi đọc được tin tức ly dị, cả 2 chỉ thấy buồn cười. Cuối buổi phỏng vấn ngắn, Peck - New 1 lần nữa khẳng định chắc nịch rằng mối quan hệ vợ chồng giữa họ vẫn đang rất bền chặt.
New Napassorn còn có đôi lời chia sẻ thêm: “Tôi chẳng bận tâm tới những thông tin không đúng sự thật. Nếu cứ phải suy nghĩ, buồn rầu vì những tin tức như vậy chắc sẽ phải khổ tâm lắm đó. Hiện tại, tôi vẫn đang rất hạnh phúc với việc chăm con và làm công việc mà mình yêu thích. Chẳng qua vì tôi là người mau nước mắt nên nhiều khán giả mới suy diễn ra thành tin đồn rạn nứt hôn nhân như vậy”.
Trước đó vào tháng 8, Peck - New cũng bất ngờ bị kéo vào nghi vấn ngoại tình gây xôn xao cả MXH xứ Thái, nhưng cặp đôi cũng đã nhanh chóng ra thông báo bác bỏ tin đồn này. Nguồn cơn của mọi chuyện bắt nguồn từ 1 thông tin ẩn danh không có danh tính cụ thể của các nhân vật chính. Theo nguồn tin này, 1 nam diễn viên hạng A Thái Lan đã bị tố lén lút ngoại tình với nữ doanh nhân xinh đẹp, quyến rũ sau lưng vợ - 1 nữ ca sĩ nổi tiếng. Đáng nói, nam tài tử trong vụ việc từ lâu đã nổi tiếng với hình tượng yêu vợ thương con bậc nhất showbiz xứ chùa vàng. Tuy nhiên, đằng sau hình ảnh đầy ngôn tình đó, nam nghệ sĩ này lại lén lút qua lại với 1 nữ doanh nhân giàu có, sở hữu diện mạo nổi bật. Nguồn tin cho biết thêm, nữ đại gia trong câu chuyện vốn là tiểu thư của 1 gia tộc lớn, là chủ sở hữu của nhà máy trị giá hàng trăm triệu Baht Thái (hàng trăm tỷ đồng). Thêm vào đó, cô từng trải qua cuộc hôn nhân với tỷ phú lớn tuổi hơn mình.
Nam diễn viên và nữ doanh nhân giàu có phát sinh mối quan hệ sai trái sau khi quen nhau tại 1 khóa học dành cho giới thượng lưu. Sau đó, nam tài tử hạng A cùng nhân tình đã lén lút hẹn hò và duy trì mối quan hệ bất chính trong suốt gần 1 năm. Cả 2 thường xuyên gặp nhau đều đặn khoảng 2 lần mỗi tuần. Người chồng luôn viện cớ với vợ rằng bản thân quá mệt mỏi vì áp lực công việc nên cần ra ngoài giải tỏa căng thẳng. Nhưng trên thực tế, anh đã lén lút đi ngoại tình với nữ đại gia sau lưng vợ. Nam diễn viên dan díu với nữ đại gia tại 1 căn hộ chung cư và nhiều lần cùng nhau đi ăn riêng tư trong bầu không khí thân mật. Nam diễn viên đình đám dường như vô cùng u mê tiểu tam giàu có. Ngoài ra, 1 nguồn tin trong giới thượng lưu cũng râm ran bàn tán rằng nữ doanh nhân nói trên còn lén lút làm tiểu tam chen chân vào mối quan hệ của nhiều cặp đôi khác nữa.
Trên các diễn đàn mạng xã hội vào thời điểm tháng 8 khi thông tin nói trên bắt đầu nổ ra, New Napassorn - Peck Premmanat đã nhanh chóng lọt vào tầm ngắm của công chúng xứ chùa vàng. Ngay giữa tâm bão đồn đoán, New Napassorn đã mạnh mẽ lên tiếng bác bỏ thông tin ông xã ngoại tình với nữ đại gia, đồng thời khẳng định gia đình họ vẫn đang rất hạnh phúc.
New tỏ ra vô cùng bức xúc khi vợ chồng cô bỗng dưng bị cuốn vào nghi vấn ngoại tình: “Chúng tôi đã sống cùng nhau được nhiều năm rồi. Từ lúc yêu nhau, kết hôn, có con và cùng xây dựng tổ ấm chung, chúng tôi đã luôn ở cạnh bên để vượt qua những khó khăn trong công việc lẫn cuộc sống. Cho đến hôm nay, tôi và ông xã vẫn còn yêu đối phương sâu đậm lắm và gia đình chúng tôi vẫn gắn bó bên nhau. Con trai chính là báu vật quan trọng nhất đối với vợ chồng tôi. Tôi buộc phải lên tiếng, bởi lẽ những thông tin đang xuất hiện tràn lan không đúng với thực tế gia đình mình. Tôi không muốn gia đình mình trở thành công cụ câu view, bị lợi dụng hay bị lôi vào những câu chuyện không hề liên quan đến mình”.
Nữ ca sĩ New Napassorn sinh năm 1983, bắt đầu trở nên nổi tiếng tại Thái Lan sau khi giành được danh hiệu Á quân tại cuộc thi tìm kiếm tài năng âm nhạc The Star mùa đầu tiên. Từ năm 2003-2023, cô hoạt động với tư cách thành viên nhóm nhạc New Jiew và gặt hái được vô số thành công. Tới năm 2024, nữ ngôi sao thành lập hãng đĩa của riêng mình mang tên Bibbidii Entertainment và chính thức trở thành CEO ở Tbiz.
Trong khi đó, Peck Premmanat kém bà xã 1 tuổi, là diễn viên, ca sĩ, người mẫu kiêm DJ nổi tiếng ở làng giải trí Thái Lan. Anh ghi dấu ấn trong nhiều bộ phim đáng chú ý như Haunted Mansion, Farm Euy Farm Ruk,...
Cặp đôi kết hôn vào năm 2017 và hạnh phúc đón con trai đầu lòng 7 năm sau đó.

articles.title: Kraken parent's acquisition of Tribe Capital flags new chapter in evolution of crypto exchanges
articles.text:
Payward, the owner of crypto exchange Kraken, is pushing into private markets with its latest acquisition, underscoring a broader shift in cryptocurrencies, from trading-led growth to the buildout of financial infrastructure.
Payward said late Wednesday that it's buying venture capital and asset management provider Tribe Capital Management, led by Payward's co-CEO Arjun Sethi. No purchase price was disclosed.
Tribe, where Sethi is co-founder and chairman, invests across early- and late-stage private companies and has $2.7 billion in assets under management.
"Joining Payward gives us the opportunity to bring Tribe's investment approach to a global financial platform," Jonathan Hsu, another co-founder of Tribe Capital, said in a statement. "We see a strong fit between our investment approach and Payward's infrastructure, distribution, and product-building capabilities."
Payward didn't respond to a request for comment.
The acquisition is novel among crypto exchanges. Unlike exchange-owned venture arms such as Coinbase Ventures or Binance Labs, Payward is looking to integrate Tribe's investment and fund-management capabilities into an existing custody, trading, collateral and tokenization infrastructure to develop private-market investment products.
Payward is trying to position itself to capture value from a broader crypto-driven transformation of financial services, not use the venture vehicle to draw more capital into the crypto ecosystem.
The acquisition is another step in the evolution in the crypto exchange business model. With cryptocurrency prices continuing to decline this year, crypto exchanges have worked to move past their reliance on trading volumes and transaction fees, focusing instead on building the infrastructure connecting digital assets with traditional finance.

articles.title: CEO SHS Nguyễn Duy Linh nhận thêm ghế Chủ tịch tại một công ty quản lý quỹ
articles.text:
CEO SHS Nguyễn Duy Linh nhận thêm ghế Chủ tịch tại một công ty quản lý quỹ
Ông Nguyễn Duy Linh, sinh năm 1982, hiện là Tổng Giám đốc Chứng khoán SHS, vừa được bầu giữ chức Chủ tịch HĐQT Công ty Cổ phần Quản lý Quỹ BVIM.
Ngày 19/11, tại Hà Nội, Công ty Cổ phần Quản lý Quỹ BVIM tổ chức Đại hội đồng cổ đông bất thường nhằm kiện toàn bộ máy lãnh đạo nhiệm kỳ 2026–2030.
Theo đó, ông Nguyễn Duy Linh, hiện là Tổng Giám đốc Công ty Cổ phần Chứng khoán Sài Gòn – Hà Nội (SHS) và thành viên HĐQT BVIM, được bầu giữ chức Chủ tịch HĐQT BVIM. Đồng thời, ông Trần Văn Mẫn được bầu bổ sung vào HĐQT công ty.
Trong đợt kiện toàn này, ông Đỗ Quang Vinh thôi giữ chức Chủ tịch HĐQT BVIM nhằm tuân thủ quy định của Luật Các tổ chức tín dụng về kiêm nhiệm chức danh quản lý, điều hành tại doanh nghiệp khác, trên tinh thần chủ động rà soát và hoàn thiện công tác quản trị của công ty.
Ông Nguyễn Duy Linh sinh năm 1982, có gần 20 năm kinh nghiệm trong lĩnh vực tài chính – chứng khoán, từng đảm nhiệm nhiều vị trí lãnh đạo cấp cao tại các công ty chứng khoán lớn ở Việt Nam.
Ông tốt nghiệp Thạc sĩ Quản trị Kinh doanh (MBA) tại Solvay Brussels School, đồng thời sở hữu bằng Cử nhân Tài chính và nhiều chứng chỉ chuyên môn về phân tích tài chính, quản trị doanh nghiệp và phát triển đội ngũ lãnh đạo.
Trước khi gia nhập SHS, ông Linh từng giữ các vị trí điều hành tại Chứng khoán VPBank (VPBankS), Chứng khoán Mirae Asset Việt Nam và Chứng khoán SSI. Kinh nghiệm của ông trải rộng từ kinh doanh chứng khoán, quản lý tài sản, ngân hàng đầu tư đến quản trị vận hành và chuyển đổi số.
Đầu năm 2026, ông Nguyễn Duy Linh được bổ nhiệm làm Tổng Giám đốc SHS trong quá trình công ty kiện toàn bộ máy điều hành và triển khai chiến lược phát triển mới.
Tại SHS, ông tham gia thúc đẩy quá trình chuyển đổi mô hình kinh doanh theo định hướng Full-Service Wealth Management, hướng tới cung cấp các dịch vụ tài chính và quản lý tài sản toàn diện.
Chiến lược này tập trung vào bốn trụ cột gồm môi giới khách hàng cá nhân và tổ chức; phân phối và tư vấn sản phẩm quản lý tài sản; ngân hàng đầu tư; đầu tư và kinh doanh nguồn vốn.
Việc ông Linh đảm nhiệm thêm vị trí Chủ tịch HĐQT BVIM được kỳ vọng góp phần tăng cường năng lực quản trị, phát triển sản phẩm đầu tư và mở rộng hoạt động quản lý tài sản, đồng thời thúc đẩy sự kết nối giữa các hoạt động ngân hàng, chứng khoán và quản lý quỹ.
Đợt kiện toàn nhân sự diễn ra trong bối cảnh thị trường quản lý tài sản tại Việt Nam tiếp tục phát triển, với nhu cầu đa dạng hóa danh mục đầu tư và sử dụng dịch vụ quản lý tài sản chuyên nghiệp ngày càng được quan tâm.

articles.title: Trận đấu của tuyển Việt Nam bất ngờ đi vào lịch sử World Cup
articles.text:
Trận đấu của tuyển Việt Nam bất ngờ đi vào lịch sử World Cup
Trận đấu giữa tuyển U17 Việt Nam gặp Bỉ sẽ đạt cột mốc chưa từng có trong lịch sử World Cup, xuất phát một diễn biến có liên quan tới trọng tài.
- 16-11-2026Thủ môn SN 2003 cao 1m91 thay Lê Giang Patrik ở đội tuyển Việt Nam
- 14-11-2026Đội tuyển Việt Nam hủy trận đấu với đương kim vô địch Asian Cup?
- 11-11-2026HLV Australia khen Đình Bắc hết lời, nhận xét ra sao về tân binh nhập tịch của tuyển Việt Nam?
Một số trang quốc tế như One Football hay Yahoo vừa đề cập tới cột mốc lịch sử ở trận đấu giữa tuyển U17 Việt Nam gặp U17 Bỉ tại lượt trận mở màn VCK U17 World Cup (diễn ra lúc 20h00 ngày 20/11 theo giờ Việt Nam).
“Một trận đấu, một khoảnh khắc lịch sử. Trận đấu giữa Bỉ và Việt Nam ở vòng mở màn bảng G tại Giải vô địch bóng đá U17 thế giới (U17 World Cup) sẽ đi vào lịch sử. Lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử, một bộ ba trọng tài người Brazil toàn nữ sẽ điều khiển một trận đấu cấp đội tuyển quốc gia nam tại World Cup. Trọng tài chính Daiane Muniz và các trợ lý Leila Cruz và Maíra Mastella Moreira sẽ đạt được cột mốc này” – One Football nhấn mạnh.
"Trước hết, xin chúc mừng họ đã đạt được cột mốc này nhờ sự kiên cường và nỗ lực cá nhân. Công việc của Liên đoàn Bóng đá São Paulo (FPF), và giờ là CBF, đã làm nổi bật khả năng bẩm sinh đáng kinh ngạc của bộ ba này. Tất cả công lao đều thuộc về họ," ông Sandro Meira Ricci, chủ tịch Ủy ban Trọng tài của Liên đoàn Bóng đá Brazil (CBF) nói về các trọng tài sẽ điều hành trận đấu của U17 Việt Nam gặp Bỉ tối nay.
Với U17 Việt Nam, chúng ta là đại diện duy nhất của khu vực Đông Nam Á giành vé tham dự U17 World Cup 2026. Đây cũng mới là lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử U17 Việt Nam giành vé dự World Cup. Đội bóng của HLV Cristiano Roland giành vé đến Qatar sau khi vượt qua vòng bảng U17 châu Á, trong đó có chiến thắng 3-2 trước UAE. Việt Nam sau đó dừng bước ở tứ kết trước Australia.
Với U17 Việt Nam, cuộc đối đầu với Bỉ sẽ mang ý nghĩa đặc biệt khi đây là trận đấu ra mắt của đội tuyển tại một kỳ U17 World Cup. Kết quả trận này cũng sẽ có tác động lớn đến cơ hội đi tiếp của thầy trò HLV Roland.
Bỉ chắc chắn là thách thức cực lớn với U17 Việt Nam, U17 Bỉ đến Qatar với tư cách á quân giải U17 châu Âu 2026, sau khi đánh bại Pháp ở bán kết và chỉ chịu thua Italy trên loạt luân lưu trong trận chung kết. Tại kỳ World Cup năm nay, Bỉ cũng đang đặt ra mục tiêu tiến vào trận chung kết.

articles.title: As Sanofi's Pompe drug shortage drags on, some patients struggle to access treatments
articles.text:
Two weeks ago, Monique Griffin got a troubling email.
The French drugmaker Sanofi told her that a shipping delay had interrupted supply of the drug that she relies on to manage her rare muscle-wasting disease. Her next infusion was canceled. Griffin, who is 51 and uses a wheelchair due to Pompe disease, fears what will happen if the shortage isn't resolved soon.
"You're basically letting the disease take over again," she said. "It's terrifying."
More than three months after initial reports of supply problems with treatments for Pompe disease, the disruption drags on, with more patients learning their infusions have been canceled. Sanofi said it has made progress restoring the supply to patients in some countries, but added that shipping delays could interrupt infusions for some U.S. patients through the end of November.
For more stories like this, sign up for the CNBC Cures newsletter.
A Sanofi spokesperson said there were no issues with drug quality and the company is "committed to ensuring that the most vulnerable patients receive treatment first during this period." The company added that patients should speak with a health professional before taking another treatment, adding, "these medicines are not interchangeable."
In a statement, the Food and Drug Administration said "patient access to these treatments is a priority for the agency and we have offered our assistance to Sanofi on anything needed to help ensure all patient needs are met."
About one in every 19,000 babies is born with Pompe disease, which is named after the Dutch pathologist who discovered the condition nearly a century ago.
Patients lack an enzyme for breaking down a complex sugar, causing a toxic buildup of glycogen inside their cells. Their muscles weaken and their heart can become enlarged. They have trouble breathing and eating. Left untreated, the disease is often fatal.
Sanofi's Lumizyme and a second-generation version, Nexviazyme, replace the missing enzyme, protecting the patient's muscles. Patients typically receive Sanofi's drugs every two weeks.
"It's a lifeline," said Jenna Yarborough, a rare disease advocate whose two children with Pompe disease have not been affected by the drug shortage.
While Pompe disease patients rely on Sanofi's drugs, several other treatments have entered clinical trials, including separate gene therapies from AskBio and Astellas Pharma.
Sanofi says the drug shortage is the result of issues at its manufacturing facility in Ireland, which public documents show the company has known about for several months. The FDA inspected the plant between January 12 and January 20, 2026 and found violations involving two unrelated drugs. The company began responding to the violations in February, but on June 22, the FDA sent the company a warning letter saying it had still not addressed the "underlying failure" to comply with manufacturing requirements. Addressing the FDA's ongoing concerns has contributed to the supply disruption of the Pompe therapies, according to Sanofi.
There's a sense of frustration within the Pompe community that the company did not do enough to warn patients about the potential for a supply disruption. Ryan Colburn, a person living with Pompe who is active in the advocacy space, says many patients were unaware of the manufacturing issues at Sanofi and were left with no way to prepare for them. "The lack of proactive transparency and apparent lack of buffer are of huge concern for any medicine that people's lives and well-being depend on access to," Colburn said.
A spokesperson for Sanofi responded, "As the situation evolved, and the extent of the disruption became clearer, we engaged global and U.S. patient advocacy organizations, patients and clinicians to inform them, and we have worked to continue to keep these groups and individuals updated through regular communications. We remain committed to continuity of care and to transparent, ongoing communication with the Pompe community as we work to stabilize supply."
Chelsey McGee's 10-year-old son Logan has taken Lumizyme every two weeks since he was diagnosed with Pompe disease as an infant. While his infusions haven't been canceled yet, she's concerned that missing even one appointment will damage his heart. Sanofi's drug has kept him healthy enough to play soccer.
"It's important that we stay on his timeline and keep his heart healthy," she said.
McGee, who lives in Minneapolis, is frustrated by what she says is a lack of transparency from Sanofi. She discovered the FDA cited the pharmaceutical company for manufacturing problems by searching the agency's website, not from the company.
Griffin, who lives in Orlando, has taken Lumizyme since 2010 when she was diagnosed with an adult-onset version of the disease. The diagnosis came after she became so fatigued that she fell while carrying groceries and suffered a concussion.
She knows what it's like to go without her infusions. She missed a few appointments earlier this year due to an insurance mix-up. She likened it to having "a really bad flu." She became extremely fatigued, struggled to breathe and started to feel pain in her legs, arms and back.
Pompe is a progressive disease, meaning it gets worse over time. She worries most about losing the strength to breathe. She sleeps with assisted ventilation.
She works in the theme parks industry and is hoping to attend a conference this week. While her Lumizyme infusions remain on hold, she hopes to get through the week of meetings "on caffeine and goodwill."
CNBC Cures is underwritten by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease and BridgeBio.
